items.title: Policymakers must prioritise durable skills for future workplaces – HP Futures 2026 report
items.description: By Elizabeth Osayande A new global report, HP Futures 2026, has urged policymakers in Nigeria and worldwide to prioritise durable skills such as creativity, critical thinking, communication and collaboration that will be essential in workplaces of the future. The report, led by HP, the Global Learning Council, and the Education Leaders Forum, convened 58 education, policymaking and future of work leaders globally to examine how education systems can equip young people for the future of work. The report called on policymakers to develop clear blueprints for helping students build durable skills and to ensure that these skills are not treated as secondary or extracurricular. According to the report, durable skills are becoming the core infrastructure of future readiness and must be resourced, timetabled and assessed accordingly. HP Futures 2026 recommends designing future skills-building programmes for public systems and low-resource contexts to ensure that durable skills do not become another source of inequality, through methods such as teacher-mediated AI, low-bandwidth delivery and predictable costs. It also called on policymakers to keep literacy, numeracy and identity-forming learning at the core of education, while using creative, hands-on approaches to deliver fundamentals and durable skills simultaneously. The report argues that durable skills must become a core part of education systems rather than an optional addition. It calls for greater support for educators, who remain central to helping students develop the creativity, critical thinking, communication, and collaboration skills that employers increasingly value. It further asks policymakers to recognise that assessment remains the biggest bottleneck to widespread building of durable skills, and that education systems need to create standardised assessment pathways for durable skills that are recognised by higher education institutions and employers across geographies. The report also argues that Nigeria and education systems worldwide should take students’ voices into account when creating durable skills-based curricula. Commenting on the findings,Chief Commercial Officer at HP and Chair of HP Futures, David McQuarrie, said: “Educators, policymakers and employers share a responsibility to prepare young people for the opportunities and challenges they will encounter throughout their lives and careers. As artificial intelligence rapidly transforms how we learn and work, that responsibility has never been more important. Education systems must do more to help students develop, demonstrate and continuously strengthen the capabilities that will remain valuable regardless of how technology evolves.” Director & Global Head Education Business and Strategy at HP, Mayank Dhingra, added: “In this report, experts call for new education models that take durable skills into account, and for students to be offered interoperable, transnational means to credentialise their durable skills so that higher education institutions and employers share a common benchmark for these crucial Future of Work abilities. Furthermore, the experts called on policymakers to take action immediately to ensure AI-era readiness and durable skills ownership does not become another source of structural inequality. “We urge policymakers and education leaders in Nigeria and around the world to review their findings, and draw on them as they work to create education systems that will set students up for success in the brave new world we are entering.” Meanwhile, the full HP Futures 2026 report can be gotten on hp website. HP Futures conducted an online survey from May to June 2026, which received 6,206 responses from students in 37 countries across versions published in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Bahasa Indonesia, Italian and Arabic. Respondents ranged from under 12 to over 25 years old, with 88 per cent of those stating an age between 12 and 17. The report also convened 58 leading experts for a series of roundtable discussions and one-to-one interviews, and compiled a series of practical case studies from schools, universities, employers, NGOs and public systems around the world. The post Policymakers must prioritise durable skills for future workplaces – HP Futures 2026 report appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Elon Musk promet une action SpaceX à chaque enfant américain dès 2027
items.description: Le milliardaire Elon Musk a annoncé vouloir offrir une action de SpaceX à chaque enfant aux États-Unis à partir de 2027. Publiée sur son réseau social X, cette déclaration reste toutefois entourée de nombreuses inconnues, le patron de l'entreprise spatiale n'ayant fourni aucun détail sur les modalités de cette initiative. Elon Musk entend-il faire profiter les plus jeunes Américains de la valeur de son entreprise spatiale ? L'homme le plus riche du monde a affirmé, lundi, vouloir donner une action de SpaceX à chaque enfant aux États-Unis dès 2027. Une annonce faite sur son réseau social X, sans précisions sur les conditions de mise en œuvre de ce projet. « L'année prochaine, je donnerai une de mes actions SpaceX à chaque enfant en Amérique » , a écrit le milliardaire dans un message succinct. Il a ajouté que cette initiative serait « la première d'une longue série » , sans expliquer comment les bénéficiaires seraient identifiés, ni selon quelles modalités les titres leur seraient attribués. À ce stade, aucun détail n'a été communiqué concernant le financement, les éventuelles conditions d'éligibilité ou la gestion de ces actions pour les mineurs. La portée concrète de cette annonce reste donc à déterminer. L'ampleur d'une telle initiative serait considérable. Selon les données démographiques américaines officielles citées dans les informations disponibles, les États-Unis comptaient environ 73 millions d'enfants et de jeunes de moins de 18 ans en 2024. Distribuer une action à chacun d'entre eux représenterait ainsi une opération de grande envergure. Sa valeur totale dépendrait notamment du nombre de titres effectivement distribués et de leur valorisation au moment du transfert. Elon Musk détient, selon les données de Forbes, environ 38 % du capital de SpaceX. Toutefois, les modalités d'une éventuelle distribution de ses propres titres, tout comme les implications juridiques et fiscales d'un tel transfert, n'ont pas été précisées. SpaceX au cœur des ambitions d'Elon Musk Fondée par Elon Musk, SpaceX occupe une place centrale dans ses ambitions spatiales, notamment en matière de transport orbital et de conquête de Mars. L'entreprise a franchi une nouvelle étape le 28 septembre, lorsque sa mégafusée Starship a atteint l'orbite terrestre pour la première fois, selon les informations rapportées. Le milliardaire a également marqué l'actualité financière avec l'entrée en Bourse de SpaceX en juin, présentée comme la plus importante de l'histoire, avec 85,7 milliards de dollars levés, selon les données mentionnées dans les informations initiales. Cette annonce intervient par ailleurs dans un contexte politique américain marqué par l'approche des élections législatives. Elle fait écho à une promesse formulée en septembre par Donald Trump, qui avait évoqué le versement d'un « dividende » de 5 000 dollars par citoyen si son parti républicain conservait le contrôle du Congrès. Elon Musk, qui a affiché son soutien au président américain, n'a cependant pas établi de lien explicite entre son projet et cette proposition politique. En l'absence de précisions supplémentaires, l'annonce d'Elon Musk doit pour l'instant être considérée comme une intention déclarée, et non comme un programme de distribution déjà détaillé. Les prochaines communications du milliardaire seront déterminantes pour comprendre les modalités et la faisabilité de cette initiative. The post Elon Musk promet une action SpaceX à chaque enfant américain dès 2027 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Judicial commission points finger at police’s ‘epic failure’, says Mir Raza was murdered
items.description: KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder case has pointed out the police’s “epic failure” in their investigation. The Sindh cabinet decided to make the report public during a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah earlier in the day. The judicial commission, which began its proceedings on Aug 28, held regular hearings to record statements of several individuals linked to the case. “This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation,” declared the 62-page report submitted by Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Justice Omar Sial, who had been heading the judicial panel. “The police breached all required procedures, both knowingly and unknowingly, necessary to withstand judicial scrutiny and a successful prosecution,” the report stated. While acknowledging that the initial police response when they were informed of the presence of a body was prompt, the report noted that subsequent events “left a lot to be desired”. “It was a murder,” the report declared. It explained that the bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound if it had been a self-inflicted injury, the “absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anaesthesia detected in the blood all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death”. The commission determined that releasing the police findings before a proper investigation was “premature and fell short of professional standards”. “Even if the death had been a suicide, the police should have established who was responsible for driving a young man to that point, including whether coercion, blackmail, or instigation was involved. They made no such effort.” It said the police investigation “failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth”. It further observed that “incessant public criticism of the police created problems” as the police “went into a shell, completely broke down communication channels, and took a position based on ego rather than on cogent, solid reasons”. The report pointed out specific issues with the police conduct: “Lack of leadership, seriousness, and supervision, and, in some cases, negligence by the senior officers. The handling of this case has been like a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination. “Ranging from negligent to criminally negligent, inexplicable, casual, and unprofessional investigation.” According to the commission, an active cover-up in the initial stages of the investigation cannot be conclusively ruled out. Referring to an Aug 9 meeting held at CM House, which “drew considerable speculation and controversy”, the report said that “no ulterior motive can be inferred from this meeting”. The meeting was attended by Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted Ali’s first autopsy, the Karachi police chief and other senior officials. Panel formed to ensure implementation The judicial panel’s primary mandate was to determine the facts and circumstances of the case; assess whether police and medico-legal investigations were impartial; identify professional negligence, misconduct, evidence manipulation, or cover-ups; review digital/forensic evidence; and recommend further investigation, forensic analysis, or legal/departmental action. According to a handout issued by the Sindh chief minister’s spokesperson, the judicial inquiry report was presented in seven separate sealed envelopes. It will be uploaded on the website of the provincial home department on Tuesday, while a copy will also be provided to the aggrieved family. Further, CM Shah also constituted a four-member sub-committee to ensure the implementation of the report. The committee comprises Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Labour Minister Saeed Ghani and the Sindh advocate general. Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon also took to X to announce that the report would be made public on Tuesday. “The government of Sindh remains committed to transparency, accountability and ensuring that due process of law is upheld,” he said. Last week, the commission handed over the sealed report to the provincial government after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings. The inquiry report, along with associated documents, was handed over to the focal person of the provincial government and Home Department Additional Secretary Javed Ahmed Abro by the commission registrar, Abdul Majid, on the premises of the SHC. After receiving the record, Abro told reporters that he would hand over the sealed report along with other records to the provincial government and it was the prerogative of the government to decide whether the inquiry report was to be brought into the public domain or otherwise. In August, the provincial government formed the commission, which was tasked with making recommendations for further investigation and forensic analysis or legal/departmental action, and it was required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sindh government within 30 days. However, the commission had struggled to meet its deadline and sent an application last month to the Sindh government for an extension in its tenure till Oct 15. Therefore, the provincial cabinet granted an extension. Besides examining 49 witnesses and available record, the commission had also sent questionnaires to Karachi police chief Azad Khan, head of current investigation team DIG Amir Farooqui and DIG East Farrukh Lanjar after dismissing an application by the aggrieved family to summon the senior police officers to testify before the commission. The 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS and his body with gunshot wounds was found a day later in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar’s locality. Initially, the police built the case around suicide on the basis of the first autopsy , which indicated a bullet entry wound on the chest, and by pointing out business losses and money borrowed by the victim. Police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had disputed the findings of the first post-mortem conducted by medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh. The second post-mortem report, however, termed its findings “inconsistent” with suicide as the manner of Mir Raza’s death. It said the Exhumation Board was of the unanimous opinion that the death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back. More to follow

items.title: Producer price inflation increases to 4.8% in September 2026
items.description: Producer Price Inflation (PPI) rose to 4.8% in September 2026, up 0.4 percentage points. Month-on-month PPI stood at 1.3%, down from 2.5% in August 2026. According to the Ghana Statistical Service, Mining and Quarrying recorded the highest index levels throughout the period, rising from 360.5 to 380.4. It recovered strongly in early 2026, fell sharply in June, and subsequently rebounded. The Extraction of Crude Oil and Natural Gas sub-sector recorded an inflation rate of 18.35. Meanwhile, inflation in the Mining of Metal Ores sub-sector fell by 1.9 percentage points, from -0.4% in August 2026 to -2.3% in September 2026. Mining Support Service Activities recorded an inflation rate of 5.3% in September 2026, down from 5.7% in August 2026. The Manufacturing Index also increased from 258.7 to 270.5, with moderate fluctuations. Eight out of the 23 major groups within the Manufacturing sub-sector recorded inflation rates above the sub-sector average of 4.6%. The Manufacture of leather and related products recorded the highest inflation rate at 15.8%, followed by the Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment at 14.3%. In contrast, the Manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products recorded deflation of 1.1 percent. Again, the Electricity, Gas, Steam and Air Conditioning Supply Index rose from 218.5 to 239.8. Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution recorded the highest inflation rate among the groups at 10.2%. This was followed by Manufacture of Gas and Distribution of Gaseous Fuels through mains, which recorded a deflation of 4.1%. The Water Supply, Sewerage, Waste Management and Remediation Activities Index increased from 162.4 to 175.8, remaining broadly stable after a marked rise in January 2026. The Construction Producer Price Index (C-PPI) also recorded an inflation rate of 4.7% in September 2026. This indicates that construction producer prices increased by 4.7% between September 2025 and September 2026. This represented an increase of 0.2 percentage points from the 4.5% recorded in August 2026. The Services Producer Price Index (S-PPI) recorded an inflation rate of 1.4 percent in September 2026. This indicates that service producer prices increased by 1.4 percent between September 2025 and September 2026. Within the sector, the Accommodation and Food Service sub-sector recorded an increase in its PPI, from 236.8 in September 2025 to 243.3 in September 2026, followed by a gradual fall to 241.8 in August 2026. Policy Implications The GSS urged household consumers to prioritise essential expenditure and adjust spending plans in response to changes in prices. It also advised them to reduce avoidable costsby adopting energy- and water-saving practices and make efficient use of household resources. For businesses and investors, it urged them to manage rising input costs , i mprove operational efficiency, strengthen cost controls and review pricing carefully to protect profitability while retaining customers. Additionally, they should maintain appropriate inventories of key inputs and diversify suppliers to reduce exposure to price increases and supply disruptions. The PPI measures the average change over time in the prices received by domestic producers for their goods and services.

Journée internationale des chefs cuisiniers : l’UCCT met les produits locaux à l’honneur
items.description: Lomé, 20 oct. (ATOP) – La quatrième édition de la journée internationale des chefs cuisiniers a été lancée le lundi 19 octobre à Lomé autour du thème national « Terre, passion, assiette ». A travers cette célébration dont le thème international est « Explorateurs culinaires », l’Union des chefs cuisiniers du Togo (UCCT) entend promouvoir la gastronomie togolaise, encourager la consommation des produits locaux et valoriser le savoir-faire des professionnels de la restauration. L’initiative vise également à favoriser la transmission des recettes traditionnelles, à stimuler la créativité des chefs et à renforcer les liens entre producteurs, transformateurs et acteurs de la restauration. Plusieurs activités sont prévues jusqu’au samedi 24 octobre. Au programme figurent des dégustations, des panels, un concours culinaire entre écoles et centres de formation, un festival du tilapia et du fonio, qui permettra de faire découvrir différentes préparations à base de ces produits du terroir. Des démonstrations culinaires et des ateliers destinés aux enfants sont aussi prévus et visent également à leur faire connaître les recettes traditionnelles et à éveiller leur intérêt pour la cuisine togolaise. Un dîner de gala marquera la fin des activités. Chef Amah Kpessou La représentante du ministre délégué chargé du Commerce et du Contrôle de la qualité, Mme Adovon Kafui a rappelé que la gastronomie constitue un patrimoine culturel et un moyen de soutenir l’économie nationale. Elle a encouragé les professionnels à utiliser davantage les produits du pays, notamment le riz, les légumes, les céréales, les épices et les produits halieutiques. Selon elle, ce choix contribue à soutenir les producteurs, les transformateurs et les commerçants, tout en favorisant la création d’emplois, particulièrement pour les jeunes et les femmes. Mme Adovon a également invité les chefs à renouveler les recettes traditionnelles en proposant des plats qui allient authenticité, créativité, qualité et accessibilité. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les relations entre les agriculteurs, les transformateurs, les commerçants, les restaurateurs, les hôteliers et les acteurs du tourisme pour faciliter l’approvisionnement en produits locaux et garantir des débouchés aux producteurs. Elle a, par ailleurs, souligné que la promotion des produits togolais doit aller de pair avec le respect des règles d’hygiène et de sécurité sanitaire des aliments. De son côté, le représentant du ministre en charge du Tourisme, Adjanou Mawuna, a salué le talent et la créativité des cuisiniers qui participent à la préservation des traditions culinaires et au développement de l’économie nationale. Selon lui, les recettes traditionnelles, les saveurs et les produits locaux offrent aux visiteurs une première découverte du pays, au même titre que ses sites touristiques, ses plages, ses cascades et ses monuments. Pour Mme Thérèse Amonah, chargée de l’organisation de l’UCCT, cette célébration est aussi une occasion de montrer les nombreuses possibilités offertes par les produits agricoles locaux. Elle a expliqué que les échanges prévus permettront de rapprocher les chefs cuisiniers des transformateurs, afin de favoriser l’utilisation des produits togolais dans les cuisines. ATOP/AO/AR

items.title: World Cup: FIFA suspends Egypt coach, forward for criticising referee after Argentina defeat
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has suspended Egypt coach Hossam Hassan for three matches and forward Mostafa Zico for five games following their criticism of the referee after the country’s 3-2 defeat by Argentina at the World Cup. According to Reuters, the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) announced the sanctions on Monday, adding that Egypt’s national team director, Ibrahim Hassan, the twin brother of Hossam, had also received a three-match suspension. Hossam was sanctioned for blaming refereeing errors for Egypt’s elimination from the tournament in the last 16, while Zico was punished for insulting the referee during a post-match interview. The EFA confirmed the disciplinary decisions in a statement, saying it had requested the detailed grounds for the sanctions from FIFA’s Disciplinary Committee to assess its legal options and determine whether to appeal. The controversy followed a disputed sequence of decisions during Egypt’s defeat to Argentina, with Zico having a goal disallowed for a foul in the build-up before Egypt’s players appealed for a penalty late in the match when the score was 2-2. However, FIFA refereeing chief Pierluigi Collina defended the officiating, warning that allegations against referees could expose them and their families to threats. The suspensions could affect Egypt’s preparations for their upcoming Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Malawi in November, with Hossam and Ibrahim Hassan potentially missing those fixtures and the opening match of the March international window. Zico’s five-match suspension could keep him out of action for Egypt until June. items.title: Sénégal : les syndicats appellent à une grève générale et le gouvernement à un dialogue
items.description: Une coalition regroupant treize syndicats sénégalais a annoncé l'organisation d'une manifestation ce mardi à Dakar, suivie d'une grève générale de 72 heures pour compter de demain mercredi, et ce malgré l'appel du gouvernement à suspendre les mouvements de protestation. Selon les médias, qui citent des responsables syndicaux, le Front syndical de défense du travail, qui regroupe notamment des organisations syndicales des secteurs de l'éducation, de la santé, de l'enseignement supérieur et de l'électricité, entend poursuivre sa mobilisation pour réclamer l'application des accords sociaux et l'amélioration des conditions de travail. Les revendications portent notamment sur la réévaluation des retraites, le relèvement de l’âge légal de la retraite de 60 à 65 ans, le versement de primes d’encouragement et la généralisation effective de l’indemnité de logement pour qu’elle atteigne 100 000 francs CFA (environ 171 dollars). Face à cette situation, huit membres du gouvernement, représentant notamment les ministères de la Justice, de l’Enseignement supérieur, de l’Éducation nationale, des Collectivités locales, de la Communication, de l’Emploi, des Transports et du Budget, ont tenu hier, lundi, une conférence de presse consacrée à l’examen des tensions sociales et des revendications syndicales. Jeudi dernier, le Premier ministre sénégalais, Ahmed Lamine Lo, avait appelé les organisations syndicales à s’engager à suspendre les grèves pendant trois mois, lors d’une réunion du comité de pilotage de la Charte nationale pour la stabilité sociale, qui rassemble des représentants du gouvernement, des employeurs et des centrales syndicales. Selon l'agence de presse sénégalaise, le Premier ministre avait proposé un mécanisme de règlement progressif des revendications, prévoyant leur traitement par les autorités compétentes, avant leur éventuel renvoi au cabinet du Premier ministre, puis à la présidence de la République pour les dossiers qui resteraient en suspens. De leur côté, les organisations syndicales réclament le respect des engagements pris par les pouvoirs publics, notamment dans le cadre de la Charte nationale pour la stabilité sociale, signée le 1er mai 2025 entre le gouvernement, les organisations patronales et les centrales syndicales.

items.title: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser
items.description: Adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) and former director general of the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) retired Lieutenant General Mazhar Jamil has warned of the “risky” outcome for South Asia and beyond of a “dangerous ideology” shaping the Indian military mindset. “Indian military thinking is being shaped by a dangerous ideology, which conflates mythology with national power. The outcome is very risky and delusional Indian military doctrines with a poor strategic sense of nuclear realities are endangering South Asia and beyond,” he said in his key note address at a workshop titled ‘Nuclear Deterrence and Strategic Stability in South Asia’. The workshop, held last week in London, was organised by the International Institute for Strategic Studies, which shared a transcript of Jamil’s address late on Monday. He began by saying that a strategic stability model for a region must take into consideration the political beliefs and strategic thinking of states, which formed the basis of policies. And that shaped the strategic and security environment in the region, he explained. “The political and strategic thinking of states, therefore, should prefer [a] political approach because military adventurism, hegemonic ambitions are highly risky and unaffordable in the South Asian nuclearised environment,” Jamil stressed, before specifically talking about India and Pakistan. The two South Asian rivals, he said, had outstanding disputes, Kashmir being the core one. “It needs to be resolved as per the United Nations Security Council resolutions. But, what we are seeing, on the contrary, is [an] Indian political approach of avoiding the resolution of conflict, because perhaps the Indian leadership believes it has no locus standi on Kashmir when it is presented on the multilateral forums,” Jamil said. He added that India “tries to manage [the] Kashmir conflict with military violence within occupied Kashmir and through military aggression against Pakistan. This has not worked, and therefore Kashmir remains a nuclear flashpoint, seriously impacting the South Asian strategic and security environment”. The security perceptions in South Asia had not evolved in a vacuum, Jamil continued. “Indian revisionist and hegemonic political aspirations have [a] long history of Indian coercion and militant violence against all [of] its neighbours. Indian political ideology is based on its mythological concept of violence and revisionism, according to which South Asia, they believe — this traditional belief — that it belongs to [the] Hindu civilisation. “And, not surprisingly, the country was given a dual name in the constitution, India, that is Bharat, clearly defining the strategic direction of the state to be Bharat,” he said. Jamil said Bharat was essentially a “revisionist concept that is rooted in reclaiming [the] vast landmass of South Asia and its domination by Hindu civilisation”. “Indian political forces, interestingly, do not shy away anymore in projecting what previous governments pursued covertly. Very surprisingly, the map of Mahabharat, the greater Bharat, as they call it, covering [the] entire landmass of South Asia, is on the display in the Lok Sabha. That’s the parliament of India, clearly giving the political direction to the state and the state organisations. “So, no wonder, beyond [the] core nuclear diet of India–Pakistan, India’s conflict with all other countries serves as a perpetual driver of [the] evolving security dynamics in South Asia,” he added. He also mentioned a recent “political transformation, led by the extremist Hindutva doctrine, that seeks to marginalise and delegitimise [the] non-Hindu population of the state, especially the Muslims”, in India. “This has introduced an additional layer of complexity to the regional security environment. This marks a significant shift towards a nationalism, which is prejudiced by extreme theological principles,” Jamil said. “So, what we see is that we have a nuclear-armed neighbour whose political and strategic thinking is subordinated to a revisionist, mythological outlook with an overconfidence to subdue its neighbours. This dangerous political philosophy has trickled into the Indian political, strategic, organisational and even societal culture.” The NCA adviser went on to say that this mindset had also, “unfortunately, penetrated deeply into Indian military thinking”. Two diametrically opposing strategic approaches Continuing his criticism, Jamil said it seemed that the Indian leadership was “frozen in time and is unable to break the shackles of history”. “Indian political- and mythological-laced stubbornness is not allowing India to realise three very fundamental but significant conclusions and lessons,” he said, adding that those lessons were vital for strategic stability in South Asia. He said the first of those lessons was that conflicts outlasted military adventurism and wars, unless they were resolved politically. “The resolution of the Kashmir conflict, therefore, needs a political approach and dialogue to achieve stability at [the] higher political planes,” he asserted. The second lesson, he said, was that any military misadventurism between two nuclear powers could only escalate the crisis to undesirable consequences and could not serve any purpose to the policy. In this connection, he added that the Indian leadership needed to understand that it “cannot dictate its unjustified and illegal policy objectives through military aggression to another nuclear power”. Moving on to the third lesson, Jamil said it was “pivotal to the crisis dynamics of South Asia”. He then cited military scholar Carl von Clausewitz, who Jamil said had warned that “war is the realm of uncertainty and escalation is really a control ladder”. Elaborating further, he said: “War is the realm of uncertainty and the lesson from the history of warfare and theory alike is clear. Wars that begin with confidence and control often end with the realisation that control was illusory. “In a nuclearised environment of South Asia, that realisation may come too late to manage safely, if [the] Indian policy of provocation with [a] false sense of achieving escalation domination continues.” Resultantly, he said, “what we are seeing in South Asia are two diametrically opposing strategic approaches, directed by the political ideology of India and Pakistan […] which define the strategic and security environment of South Asia”. The Indian strategic approach, he said, sought political and military dominance to be a “regional hegemon with a revisionist political thinking”. Whereas Pakistan’s strategic approach was directed at the resolution of conflicts through a political process with shared prosperity and to defend the sovereignty with strength against a “regional bully”, he added. ‘Irresponsible nuclear behaviour’ He then shared his views on how the global geopolitical environment and emerging destructive technologies were impacting the strategic stability of South Asia. “To me, there are three major outcomes of [the] contemporary global strategic environment that have influenced [the] Indian leadership’s strategic thinking and behaviour,” he said. He said first of those outcomes was that in the Asia-Pacific balance-of-power struggle, India presented itself as a net security provider, to exploit this geopolitical competition for its own global power-projection ambitions. “The US and Western powers did not dig deep into the actual political motives and capacity of India, [and] rather were too quick to grant this status to India. This, however, gave India a false sense of hegemony in the region,” he said. The second outcome, Jamil said, pertained to the support by Indian technology partners and, “very strangely, also allowing India to get a Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver , in spite of its irresponsible nuclear behaviour”. “Resultantly, India, now, is running one of the fastest-growing nuclear and missile programmes. This has been done with no regard and concern to arms control, a key factor in the strategic stability for the region. So, we now see India developing intercontinental ballistic missiles and submarine-launched ballistic missiles to reach the entire globe, with eight reactors outside International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards.” Pointing out that India was not a party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, he said its reactors outside IAEA safeguards “are operating as a potential source of fissile material for nuclear weapons”. “From the nuclearisation of South Asia in 1974 to the nuclearisation of the Indian Ocean by Bharat speaks of its global power ambitions. I think what [we] should now worry about is this ambitious and revisionist state reaching to most of their capitals with no restraints and transparency, even to its own technology partners,” Jamil said. He said the third outcome was about the policy of appeasement by “certain powers that has made India think that its exceptionalism will always be acceptable to the world”. “Indian propaganda and [its] disinformation campaign was accepted without scrutiny and responsibility. No questions [were] asked to India about its human-rights violations in Kashmir and against minorities, where state institutions and Hindu extremists [are] conducting heinous crimes as a state policy,” he said, adding that it was only a matter of time before internal uprising in India-occupied Kashmir boiled over. “That will have a serious impact on the security and stability of our region,” he warned. In parallel, he said, India’s access to advanced technologies, space-based capabilities, dual-use weapons systems were also impacting strategic stability. “Dual-use platforms with precision-guided systems have blurred the lines between conventional and nuclear technologies, making it more dangerous for South Asia, due to its geographical proximities and also the sensitivities”. “This also has to be seen against the backdrop of the irresponsible behaviour of India. The case in point is the intentional BrahMos missile attack on Pakistan on 9 March 2022. Strangely, it took India 48 hours to tell its nuclear neighbour about this incident,” Jamil recalled. He added, “While India claimed this to be an accident, it speaks volumes about the dysfunctionality of Indian command-and-control systems, and maybe the presence of some rogue elements in their organisation, because India never shared the findings of [its] investigations for [the] sake of transparency and building some trust.” Likewise, the launch of dual-capable BrahMos missiles during the four-day military conflict between Indian and Pakistan in May 2025 “was a deliberate act of provocation that could have caused catastrophic miscalculation”, Jamil said. “So, it complicates the regional security dynamics, which already lacks institutionalised confidence-building measures and an arms-control mechanism aligned with the emerging technologies.”

items.title: Coopération Sénégal–Côte d’Ivoire : le Premier ministre reçu par Alassane Ouattara et Tiémoko Meyliet Koné
items.description: Au terme de sa visite de travail de 24 heures à Abidjan, le Premier ministre sénégalais, Ahmadou Alhaminou Lô, a été reçu par le président ivoirien, Alassane Ouattara, et le vice-président, Tiémoko Meyliet Koné. Les échanges ont porté sur les moyens de renforcer la coopération entre le Sénégal et la Côte d’Ivoire, notamment dans les domaines de la sécurité, du commerce, de l’agriculture et des politiques publiques. Ces secteurs occupent une place importante dans les relations entre les deux pays. Le renforcement des échanges commerciaux, la coopération en matière de sécurité et le partage d’expériences dans la conduite des politiques publiques figurent parmi les pistes évoquées pour approfondir leur partenariat. Cette visite s’inscrit dans la volonté de Dakar et d’Abidjan de consolider leurs liens historiques d’amitié et de solidarité. Les deux pays entendent aussi renforcer leur concertation et développer des actions communes en faveur du développement économique et social, ainsi que de l’intégration régionale en Afrique de l’Ouest. À travers ces audiences au sommet de l’État ivoirien, le Sénégal réaffirme son engagement en faveur d’une coopération fondée sur le dialogue et la recherche de réponses communes aux défis de la région. Cette étape de la visite vise ainsi à donner un nouvel élan à l’axe Dakar-Abidjan et à renforcer un partenariat au bénéfice des deux pays. C.G.D

items.description: IGNITE Social Enterprise has announced the expansion of its lifestyle and wellness product ecosystem alongside the official unveiling of its Global Advisory Board, featuring Ghanaian media icon and CEO of EIB Network Group, Nathan Kwabena Anokye Adisi, popularly known as Bola Ray. The announcement was made on stage during a regional launch event at the Atlantis Dubai, underscoring IGNITE’s mission to connect African micro-entrepreneurs, digital creators, and trade leaders to global social commerce pipelines. Advancing Ghana’s Digital Economy and Entrepreneurial Landscape Ghana continues to establish itself as a prominent hub for youth-led enterprise, digital commerce, and innovation across West Africa. As informal trade transitions rapidly into structured digital economies, IGNITE’s social commerce model provides micro-entrepreneurs and brand affiliates with structured training, turn-key digital tools, and consumer product lines to build resilient independent businesses. The appointment of Nathan Kwabena Anokye Adisi (Bola Ray) places an influential Ghanaian voice at the strategic core of IGNITE’s global roadmap. Known for driving creative enterprise, media innovation, and youth empowerment across the continent, Bola Ray bridges local market dynamics with global trade strategy. “Across Ghana and Africa, thousands of ambitious individuals are seeking practical pathways to acquire digital skills, launch viable businesses, and generate sustainable wealth,” said Bola Ray, Global Advisory Board Member at IGNITE. “IGNITE is not merely introducing consumer items; it is architecting an enduring socio-economic ecosystem. By pairing a practical AI-based learning platform with curated, high-demand lifestyle products, we are unlocking meaningful earning avenues for local entrepreneurs and elevating African participation in the global marketplace.” Unveiling a Strengthened Lifestyle and Wellness Product Portfolio On stage at the Atlantis Dubai, IGNITE revealed four core product lines engineered to address everyday modern lifestyle, skin health, and wellness needs: Aria Wellness Pendant: Designed around Sanarey Fusion Technology (SFT), Aria features a calibrated activated wafer core utilising frequency coherence to address environmental electromagnetic and 5G exposure, support biofield balance, focus, and recovery. BRIGHT Skincare: A premium skincare range developed in South Korea, formulated with high-performance Polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) regenerative compounds and cutting-edge skincare science. SENA Timepieces: A line of Malaysian-assembled automatic watches blending heritage craftsmanship with everyday durability, built with Japanese Miyota movements, sapphire crystal, and 316L surgical stainless steel. brAInify, AI-Powered Digital Learning: Specialised digital tools and AI-driven skill acquisition modules tailored to help affiliates navigate modern social selling, customer acquisition, and business management. Product rollouts across West African territories will be introduced systematically in alignment with local regulatory approvals and market readiness. Strategic Global Governance The IGNITE Global Advisory Board serves as an independent consultative body guiding ethical corporate governance, sustainable expansion, and cross-border trade ethics across Asia, the Middle East, and Sub-Saharan Africa. Chaired by Malaysian corporate leader Dato’ Sri Subahan Kamal, the board unites interdisciplinary leaders including: Dr Konstantin Korotkov , biophysicist, pioneer of electro-photonic imaging, and developer of the Bio-Well system. Dr Beverly Rubik, PhD , biophysicist, biofield researcher, and former advisory panel chair at the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH). Nathan Kwabena Anokye Adisi (Bola Ray) , CEO of EIB Network Group and founder of Empire Group. “As IGNITE scales across Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, our growth must remain grounded in ethical transparency and tangible socio-economic value for the communities we enter,” said Dato’ Sri Subahan Kamal, Chairman of the IGNITE Global Advisory Board. “Bola Ray’s deep insight into African enterprise and youth culture will ensure IGNITE’s footprint in Ghana and across the continent is built on a sustainable, long-term foundation.” About IGNITE Social Enterprise Founded in 2026 and headquartered in Hong Kong, IGNITE is a global social enterprise that helps micro-entrepreneurs grow their businesses through an innovative social e-commerce model that combines high-quality products and future-ready services. Driven by the mission to Own Your Future , IGNITE provides individuals worldwide with modern digital tools, training, and premium wellness and lifestyle product lines designed to support financial independence, personal growth, and professional success.

items.title: Un satélite ruso acecha a otro de EE UU durante días en una maniobra “sin precedentes”: un paso más hacia la guerra de las galaxias
items.description: El clima belicista que sobrevuela la geopolítica terrestre comienza a cristalizar en el espacio. Hace unas semanas, EE UU reconoció por primera vez que tenía armas activas “en órbita”. Y en los últimos días, Rusia también ha enseñado los dientes en el espacio al acosar al satélite Iceye-X36, un artefacto comercial de propiedad estadounidense que proporciona a Ucrania imágenes muy nítidas de los escenarios de la guerra que libra contra las tropas de Vladímir Putin. El satélite ruso Kosmos-2612 comenzó a finales de septiembre una serie de sospechosas maniobras que culminaron el pasado 18 de octubre, acercándose hasta un punto de “extrema proximidad” mientras recorrían la Tierra a 540 kilómetros de altura, poniendo en peligro la integridad del artefacto. Los especialistas en tráfico espacial consideran la persecución una maniobra de una agresividad inédita. La sombra de los sabotajes que hoy recorre Europa también llega al espacio con un claro significado geopolítico: un satélite militar ruso se ha acercado extraordinariamente a un satélite comercial estadounidense que presta apoyo militar a Ucrania. items.title: UN condemns deadly drone strikes on Sudan civilians
items.description: The United Nations has condemned drone attacks that have killed at least 48 civilians in Blue Nile and West Kordofan, including women and children sheltering after fleeing their homes, and called for accountability and respect for international humanitarian law. The United Nations has condemned a series of deadly drone strikes on displaced civilians in Blue Nile and West Kordofan, warning that people fleeing Sudan’s war are being exposed to further violence in places where they sought safety. United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Sudan, Denise Brown (Photo: UN) Denise Brown, the UN resident and humanitarian coordinator in Sudan, said she was “horrified” by reports of a drone strike near a displacement site in Wad El Mahi, Blue Nile State, where at least 31 civilians, mostly women and children, were killed and dozens more injured. Some of the injured are in a serious condition, and the death toll could rise. The victims had been displaced by recent fighting in Geissan and Kurmuk localities. Brown said the area, which is under the control of the Sudanese Armed Forces, had come under attack during the preceding week. Condemning the killings, Brown called for accountability for what she described as a flagrant disregard for international humanitarian law. Logo of the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) “Those who disregard international humanitarian law need to be held accountable,” she said, stressing that the law protects civilians as well as the humanitarian and medical personnel serving them. In a separate statement, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) expressed deep concern over two drone strikes in West Kordofan on 9 October. At least 12 civilians, including women and children, were reportedly killed and eight injured when a drone struck a building sheltering displaced families in El Nuhud. A second strike in Ghubeish reportedly killed five civilians, including three children, in a residential neighbourhood hosting displaced families. “These were people who had already been forced from their homes by conflict, only to face further violence in places where they had sought safety,” OCHA said. The agency warned that the increasing frequency of drone strikes across Sudan was exposing civilians, particularly displaced families, to further death, injury and suffering. It called on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. Brown said continued attacks in Blue Nile had displaced thousands of civilians in recent weeks, exposing many more to death, direct harm and further hardship. She also criticised the international community for allowing the suffering of Sudan’s population to continue. The latest attacks follow other deadly drone strikes on civilian areas and displacement shelters across the country, as reported by Radio Dabanga today. items.title: PPI for September 2026 increases to 4.8%
items.description: The Producer Price Index (PPI) for September 2026 increased to 4.8 percent from 3.3 percent year on year. By this, the PPI, which measures the average change over time in the prices received by domestic producers for their goods and services increased for September this year compared to the same period last year. A statement released by the Ghana Statistical Service said the Industrial Producer Price Index (I-PPI) inflation rate for September 2026 was 7.2 percent, indicating that, on average, industrial producer prices increased by 7.2 percent between September 2025 and September 2026. This represents an increase of 0.9 percentage points from the 6.3 percent recorded in August 2026. The Construction Producer Price Index recorded an inflation rate of 4.7 percent in September 2026. This indicates that construction producer prices increased by 4.7 percent between September 2025 and September 2026. This represents an increase of 0.2 percentage points from the 4.5 percent recorded in August 2026. The Services Producer Price Index recorded an inflation rate of 1.4 percent in September 2026. This indicates that service producer prices increased by 1.4 percent between September 2025 and September 2026. The Services sector remained relatively stable over the review period, with the Producer Price Index increasing marginally from 142.9 in September 2025 to 144.9 in September 2026. Meanwhile, Information and Communication remained the most stable sub-sector over the period, ending at 127.8 in September 2026. items.title: US VP Vance says he is staying out of Israel vote as Trump backs Netanyahu
items.description: US Vice President JD Vance said he would not be following Donald Trump in endorsing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and wanted to stay on the sidelines. “I’m not anti-endorsing him. I’m not pro-endorsing him. I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” Vance said of Netanyahu, in an interview on Monday with journalist Mark Halperin. “I endorse American candidates and that’s where I’m focused on is the (US) midterms,” he added. Trump on Sunday issued a public endorsement of his right-wing ally Netanyahu, who is seeking a new term as premier in Israel’s Oct 27 parliamentary election. Vance’s reticence to weigh in on the Israeli vote contrasts with his approach to European elections . Days before Hungary’s parliamentary election in April, he flew to Budapest to support then-prime minister Viktor Orban , another right-wing figure. He has also voiced support for Germany’s far-right AfD party , whose leader, Alice Weidel , he met last year. Vance, who is widely viewed as aiming to succeed Trump in 2029, reportedly expressed opposition to launching the US-Israeli war with Iran, but has since defended the campaign. The vice president also had notably strong words for Israeli officials who criticised a short-lived US-Iran ceasefire agreement in June. “Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment,” he said at the time. “If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world,” he added.

items.title: Après plus de cinq mois de crise, la Roumanie a un gouvernement
items.description: Cinq mois et demi après la chute du gouvernement d’Ilie Bolojan, renversé par une motion de censure le 5 mai, la Roumanie s’est dotée aujourd’hui, mardi 20 octobre, d’un nouveau gouvernement. Luca Niculescu, premier ministre désigné le 5 octobre par le président Nicușor Dan, a obtenu 280 voix, selon Digi24, soit 47 de plus que les 233 requises Guvernul propus de Luca Niculescu a trecut de votul Parlamentului », Digi24 , 20 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Niculescu, ancien ambassadeur roumain à Paris, est le quatrième Premier ministre désigné par Dan depuis mai, après Eugen Tomac, Adrian Veștea et Siegfried Mureșan. Ce dernier, issu du PNL et vice-président du PPE, avait été désigné après deux tentatives infructueuses consécutives à la chute du gouvernement Bolojan, renversé par un vote commun PSD/AUR. Il a échoué fin septembre à obtenir la confiance du Parlement, n’ayant recueilli que 182 voix, soit 51 de moins que les 233 requises. Ni le PNL ni l’UDMR n’entreront au gouvernement, mais les deux partis avaient annoncé voter en faveur de l’investiture de Niculescu. L’AUR, l’USR et le SOS Roumanie, qui disposent respectivement de 92, 58 et 13 sièges au Parlement, avaient annoncé qu’ils ne le soutiendraient pas. Bolojan, qui avait assuré la présidence par intérim du pays après la démission de Klaus Iohannis en février 2025, et qui siège au Sénat dans les rangs du PNL, dont il est le président, a justifié le soutien de son parti par un « vote de nécessité ». Celui-ci a reproché au PSD et à l’AUR d’avoir renversé « de manière irresponsable » son gouvernement, sans proposer de « solution viable » en remplacement. Le gouvernement Niculescu devra faire face à une situation budgétaire dégradée ainsi qu’à la menace croissante que fait peser la Russie de Poutine sur la souveraineté et la sécurité du pays. La Roumanie est le pays de l’Union ayant le déficit public le plus important (7,9 % du PIB en 2025). Dans son programme, Niculescu s’est engagé à le ramener en dessous de 3 % du PIB d’ici 2030, via la limitation des dépenses, des mesures de lutte contre la fraude fiscale et l’amélioration du recouvrement des recettes. Son gouvernement est surtout composé de ministres issus du PSD. Le pays est aussi en première ligne face aux menaces russes, qui sont de plus en plus nombreuses : sept navires commerciaux ont été attaqués au large de la Roumanie et de la Bulgarie depuis le début du mois. Samedi 17 octobre, deux F-16 ayant décollé de la base de Borcea ont abattu deux drones d’attaque de type Geran, utilisés par l’armée russe. items.title: ADC asks Rivers Assembly to explain reversal of vacancy declaration against 3 pro-Fubara lawmakers
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has asked the Rivers State House of Assembly to explain the legal basis for reversing its earlier decision declaring the seats of three lawmakers vacant after reportedly notifying the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct by-elections. The affected lawmakers are Hon. Victor Oko-Jumbo, Bonny State Constituency, Hon. Sokari Goodboy Sokari, Ahoada West and Hon. Timothy Oruibienimigha, Opobo/Nkoro, who were strong allies of Governor Siminalayi Fubara. It would be recalled that the state assembly led by Hon. Martin Amaewhule, on Monday, resolved to rescind its declaration of the seats of the trio vacant following the political crisis that rocked the state. However, in a statement in Port Harcourt on Tuesday, signed by the State Publicity Secretary of ADC, Chizy Enyi Esq., the party bemoaned the assembly’s decision, stating that it raises questions about the consistency of the house in decision-making and adherence to constitutional provisions. Enyi said the Assembly had initially relied on constitutional provisions to declare the seats vacant but subsequently reversed the decision following letters of apology and explanations from the affected lawmakers. He questioned whether the initial declaration was constitutionally valid and, if so, what legal authority empowered the Assembly to reverse it, urging the lawmakers to explain why the seats were declared vacant if the initial action was defective. Citing Section 109 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Enyi enjoined the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Martin Chike Amaewhule, to clarify the legal grounds for both decisions and state whether the requirements governing justified absence from legislative sittings were duly observed. The spokesman further called for clarification on whether INEC had been formally notified of the reversal and what implications it had for any electoral processes initiated following the earlier declaration. He questioned whether the decision was reached independently or influenced by recent political reconciliation efforts involving the Minister of Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, and Governor Fubara. Enyi, while acknowledging that a legislative house could reconsider previous resolutions on legitimate grounds, maintained that such powers must be exercised within the confines of the Constitution. He, however, advised the Assembly to make relevant proceedings, attendance records and other supporting documents available for public scrutiny, adding that unresolved constitutional issues should be referred to the appropriate judicial authorities. Enyi added that political reconciliation should not override constitutional compliance, stressing that Rivers people deserved a legislature guided by due process and public interest. items.title: Un poète mauritanien primé lors de la 2ème édition du concours « villes de poèmes »
items.description: L'Organisation islamique pour l'éducation, les sciences et la culture (ISESCO) a annoncé que le poète mauritanien Sidi Mohamed Mohamed El-Mahdi avait remporté un prix d'honneur lors de la deuxième édition du concours « Villes de poèmes ». Cette édition était consacrée à la ville de Samarcande, en Ouzbékistan, afin de célébrer son statut de capitale de la culture du monde islamique pour l'année 2025. Le poète mauritanien figure parmi les sept poètes ayant reçu des prix d’honneur, aux côtés des lauréats des trois premières places, dans le cadre d’un concours visant à célébrer les villes et les civilisations à travers la poésie, et à mettre en valeur leur histoire ainsi que leur mémoire culturelle et humaine. Selon l’ISESCO, le jury du concours a reçu 600 poèmes, parmi lesquels 174 ont été sélectionnés pour participer aux différentes étapes de l’évaluation, avant l’annonce des résultats finaux. Le concours « Villes de poèmes » vise à renforcer le lien entre la poésie et le lieu, à documenter l’histoire et la géographie des villes par la poésie, et de mettre en valeur les symboles et les civilisations que les capitales culturelles du monde islamique ont accueillis.

items.title: Former Manchester United forward Dwight Yorke confirms interest in Black Stars coaching job
items.description: Former Manchester United forward Dwight Yorke has openly confirmed his interest becoming the next Black Stars head coach. Yorke is among the notable names linked with the vacant role following the departure of former coach Carlos Queiroz. The Portuguese mutually parted ways with the Ghana Football Association (GFA) following a difficult start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers, which included a 2-0 defeat away to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké and a 4-2 loss at home to Gambia. Speaking to The Guardian, Yorke stated that the team’s immense talent makes the role an attractive prospect, provided the right team culture and player commitment are established. “It’s a job I’d be interested in, given Ghana’s history and the players available,” Yorke said. “You look at the squad, and your eyes open even wider. The conversation [I had with an agent regarding my interest in coaching the Black Stars] started there and then reached the media before I really knew it. “The talent is there. Build the culture and get the players to buy in, and the football will follow.” Yorke served as the head coach of the Trinidad and Tobago national team from November 2024 to March 2026. Prior to joining Trinidad and Tobago, the former United striker coached Australian top-flight side Macarthur Football Club, penning a two-year deal in July 2022 before being sacked in 2023. In the wake of Queiroz’s exit, the GFA and the Ministry of Youth and Sports selected an interim technical team to manage the camp. Black Queens head coach Kim Lars Björkegren has been placed in charge as interim head coach, supported by assistant coaches Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram, alongside former national team goalkeeper Fatawu Dauda as goalkeeper trainer. The interim team will guide the team for the 2027 AFCON qualifier doubleheader against Somalia in November. The Black Stars currently find themselves at the bottom of the Group C table without a point after two matches. Having missed out on the 2025 AFCON, the pressure is firmly on the team to win their upcoming matches.

items.title: Mondial U17 féminin : le Maroc affronte l’Allemagne pour la deuxième journée
items.description: Les Lioncelles de l’Atlas affrontent l’Allemagne ce mardi 20 octobre à 18h, au Complexe Mohammed VI de football à Maâmora, pour la deuxième journée de la Coupe du monde féminine U17 2026. La rencontre sera diffusée sur Arryadia, beIN Sports et FIFA+. Après leur entrée en lice réussie face à la Nouvelle-Zélande (4-0), les Lioncelles de l’Atlas s’apprêtent à relever un nouveau défi. La sélection marocaine U17 affronte l’Allemagne, ce mardi à partir de 18h, dans le cadre de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes du Mondial féminin U17, organisé au Maroc du 17 octobre au 7 novembre 2026. Les Marocaines ont marqué les esprits lors de leur premier match en s’imposant largement grâce aux réalisations de Sonia Abaijou (57e), à un but contre son camp d’Eden Chaytor (70e), d’Imane Dhissi (76e) et de Hiba Youssoufi sur penalty (82e). De son côté, l’Allemagne a également débuté la compétition par une victoire, en renversant l’Argentine sur le score de 2-1. Cette confrontation s’annonce donc importante pour les deux équipes dans la course à la qualification pour la phase à élimination directe. Le match se disputera au Complexe Mohammed VI de football à Maâmora, avec un coup d’envoi prévu à 18h, heure marocaine. Leader de son groupe après sa victoire inaugurale, la sélection marocaine tentera de confirmer son bon départ devant son public et de consolider ses chances de qualification pour le tour suivant. items.title: ‘My officers are suffering’ – Director-General of Prisons calls for welfare interventions
items.description: The Director-General of the Ghana Prisons Service, Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, has described the conditions under which some prison officers work as “hell”, appealing for welfare interventions, including a contagious disease allowance, to improve their working conditions and protect their well-being. She has appealed to the Public Accounts Committee t to improve conditions of service for prison officers, particularly through better remuneration and the introduction of a contagious disease allowance for officers exposed to potentially infectious inmates. Speaking before the committee on Tuesday, October 20, Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie said prison officers endured difficult working conditions despite not having committed any criminal offence themselves. “The Ghana Prison Service, working as a prison officer, is hell. It has a psychological effect, emotional effect, physical effect,” she said. She explained that prison officers were required to work and live in the same environment as convicted persons, exposing them to many of the difficult conditions associated with incarceration. “Everything about a prison officer is highly challenging, because the prison officer, who is not convicted of any offence, is compelled to live in the same space as somebody who is convicted,” she said. According to her, the consequences of these conditions extend beyond the workplace, with the average prison officer facing considerable psychological pressure. “What it means is that every bad condition in that environment is directly linked to the prison officer, who has not committed any offence. So the average prison officer is usually depressed,” she added. Poor conditions threaten recruitment Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie also raised concerns about the Ghana Prisons Service’s ability to attract qualified and motivated personnel, pointing to recruitment trends that she said suggested a lack of interest in joining the service. She said the number of people who sought to purchase recruitment forms for the Prisons Service was significantly lower than the figures recorded for other security agencies during the last recruitment exercise. She warned that the trend should concern policymakers, as it suggested that prospective applicants were increasingly reluctant to pursue careers in the service. “The last recruitment that we did, when you look at the trend of how people purchase the forms, gave me a very serious implication, or a concern, because the people who wanted to buy the prison forms were far fewer than all the other agencies, which means that people are not ready to be prison officers,” she said. The Director-General attributed the situation to the difficult working environment and what she described as inadequate salaries. She argued that the country needed to recognise the risks and demands associated with prison work and provide additional compensation to make the profession more attractive. “Because the environment is toxic, the salary is not too good, and we must begin to compensate for these things as part of salary as a country,” she said. She added that improving remuneration and conditions of service was necessary to attract the right people to the service and ensure that officers could effectively carry out their responsibilities. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie expressed hope that her appeal to the committee would help the public and policymakers better appreciate the challenges facing prison officers and the need for urgent support. Call for contagious disease allowance A major concern raised by the Director-General was the long-standing demand for a contagious disease allowance for prison officers who face the risk of exposure to infectious diseases while performing their duties. She said the issue had been under consideration for a considerable period, but argued that the current approach to the allowance did not adequately address the risks confronting officers across the prison system. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie noted that allowances were paid to personnel at Ankaful Prison because the facility had been designated as a contagious disease prison. However, she maintained that the greatest risk could lie elsewhere, particularly in facilities where the health status of inmates had not yet been established. She explained that prisoners sent to a designated contagious disease facility would generally have been diagnosed with a relevant illness before their transfer. Officers working in other prison facilities, by contrast, could be exposed to infectious diseases before the conditions of inmates were identified. “For me, the biggest challenge is not those who are even working in the contagious disease prison. Because by the time we are taking a prisoner there, we would have diagnosed him as having a disease,” she said. “The danger, rather, is in the spaces where we are yet to know whether the prisoners have the contagious disease or not.” She argued that officers working in these settings should also be considered for the allowance because they could face exposure while caring for inmates whose medical status remained unknown. “They, rather, are not being paid that allowance. So it’s a very humble appeal,” she told the committee. Appeals for targeted financial support The Director-General urged PAC to prioritise addressing this gap in the allowance system, arguing that the financial implications would be relatively small compared with the potential benefits for officers’ welfare. She said the government and relevant authorities could begin by resolving the issue of the contagious disease allowance before considering broader salary-related concerns. “The margin is very little. I believe that before we look at all other salaries, if we can work on that, at least it will be a step in the right direction to ensure that my officers are somehow taken good care of,” she said. Mrs Baffoe-Bonnie maintained that better welfare arrangements would not only improve the well-being of prison officers but also strengthen their ability to discharge their duties in accordance with the law. She said providing officers with appropriate support would give her greater confidence in enforcing the law while ensuring that personnel were not left to bear the burden of difficult working conditions without adequate compensation. “And I’ll have the moral courage and justification to be implementing the laws as they are,” she said. The Director-General reiterated her appeal to PAC to consider the concerns raised and take steps to improve the welfare of prison officers.

items.title: Customs seeks review of N1.68trn import duty waivers
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Nigeria Customs Service has called for a review of import duty concessions valued at N1.68 trillion, warning that poorly targeted waivers could undermine government revenue at a time the Federal Government is seeking to strengthen public finances and expand funding for essential services. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the concessions granted in 2024 needed to be examined to determine whether they were achieving their intended economic objectives or unnecessarily depriving the government of revenue. Adeniyi spoke on Tuesday at the third Distinguished Personality Lecture of the TETFund Centre of Excellence in Security Management, University of Ibadan, Oyo State, where he delivered a lecture titled, “Why Customs Matters: Revenue, Security and Nationhood in a Borderless World.” He said the review should form part of a broader effort to strengthen revenue collection through improved compliance, digitalisation, intelligence-led enforcement and more transparent trade procedures. The Customs chief disclosed that the Service generated N7.28 trillion in 2025, exceeding its target of N6.58 trillion, while collections reached approximately N4.03 trillion in the first half of 2026 against an annual target of N11.07 trillion. He said the figures demonstrated the growing importance of Customs to Nigeria’s public finances and the need to close revenue leakages without placing unnecessary burdens on legitimate businesses. Adeniyi said Customs revenue was not merely a federal government resource, explaining that import duties contributed to the Federation Account and were distributed among the three tiers of government. Under the allocation formula he cited, the Federal Government receives 52.68 per cent, states 26.72 per cent and local governments 20.60 per cent. He added that, under the new tax laws, 90 per cent of value-added tax collected on imports was allocated to states and local governments. “When a smuggler evades duty, he does not cheat an abstraction called government. He cheats a pupil, a nurse and a farmer,” he said. Adeniyi traced the Service’s revenue growth from N3.2 trillion in 2023 to N6.105 trillion in 2024 and N7.28 trillion in 2025, attributing the improvement to stronger compliance, improved valuation, digital systems and enforcement. He said the Service was determined to meet its 2026 target by reducing revenue leakages rather than obstructing legitimate trade. “We will pursue the target through compliance, data and facilitation, not through harassment at the ports, because a target met by choking trade would be a false victory,” he said. The Customs chief also cited the need to address illicit financial flows and trade misinvoicing, through which importers and exporters manipulate the declared value or description of goods to evade taxes, duties and other financial obligations. He said such practices weakened the country’s revenue base and undermined the integrity of its trade system. Adeniyi noted that Africa’s tax-to-GDP ratio stood at about 16.1 per cent, compared with approximately 33.9 per cent for countries in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, highlighting the continent’s broader challenge of mobilising domestic revenue. He said Customs had a critical role to play in closing the gap by improving the accuracy of declarations, strengthening risk assessment and ensuring that eligible transactions were properly assessed. Adeniyi said the Service was deploying digital platforms and data analytics to improve the assessment of imports, detect suspicious declarations and reduce delays at the ports. He disclosed that the B’Odogwu cargo-processing platform handled approximately 16,000 entries and generated N120 billion in revenue in its first three months at the Port and Terminal Multi-Services Limited Command. He said the National Single Window, which went live on March 27, 2026, was intended to connect trade-related government processes and reduce duplication in documentation. “A study conducted at Tin Can Island Port showed that cargo release took almost five days on average, with more than 90 per cent of the time spent waiting.“ The Service, he said, was working towards reducing cargo clearance to 24 hours in the long term, with an interim target of two days and a plan to rely on scanning rather than physical examination for 99 per cent of cargo. He added that 51 companies certified under the Authorised Economic Operator programme had reduced their clearance time from 168 hours to 41 hours, while demurrage costs fell by approximately 90 per cent. According to him, the improvements showed that revenue collection and trade facilitation could reinforce each other when procedures were efficient and compliance was properly managed. Adeniyi said revenue protection could not be separated from national security, citing the interception of 399 pump-action rifles and hundreds of firearm components concealed in a container discharged from the vessel MV Velika at Tin Can Island Port in July 2026. The weapons were handed over to the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons, while the case remained before the Federal High Court. He also recalled the seizure of 844 rifles and 112,500 rounds of ammunition at Onne, Rivers State, in June 2024, as well as the handover of 1,599 firearms seized between 2018 and 2024 to the national centre in February 2025. The Customs chief said the Service had also intercepted 25 containers of fake and unregistered medicines worth approximately N9.2 billion in July 2025. On wildlife trafficking, he cited the seizure of 3.76 tonnes of pangolin scales in Lagos in April 2025, representing at least 1,900 animals, and said enforcement operations since 2021 had led to seizures of more than 25 tonnes of pangolin scales and over one tonne of ivory, with 12 convictions secured. He also highlighted fuel smuggling, drug trafficking and the illegal movement of food commodities as activities that threatened public safety, economic stability and government revenue. On border management, Adeniyi argued that intelligence-led enforcement and cooperation with neighbouring countries were more sustainable than blanket border closures. He said Nigeria’s land-border closure between August 2019 and December 2020 curtailed some smuggling activities but did not eliminate the networks behind the illegal trade. “The lesson is that a nation is protected by intelligent control of its border, not by sealing it. Closure is a blunt instrument, while intelligence, data and joint patrols with our neighbours are sharper ones,” he said. He called for closer cooperation with border communities and neighbouring countries, while urging traders to use legitimate channels under regional trade arrangements such as the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme. Adeniyi also said Nigeria’s participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area depended on effective customs administration to verify the origin of goods and ensure that preferential trade arrangements were properly implemented. Imports from other African countries accounted for approximately four per cent of Nigeria’s total imports in 2025, he said, suggesting significant room for expanding intra-African trade. The Comptroller-General proposed a structured partnership with the University of Ibadan’s Centre of Excellence in Security Management to improve research on border economies, trade compliance and illicit financial flows. His proposals included a Border Economies Research Partnership focusing on locations such as Idiroko, Seme, Jibia and Illela; Customs Data and Analytics Fellowships; and an Illicit Trade Observatory to track trafficking in firearms, drugs, counterfeit medicines, wildlife products and fuel. He also called for independent academic evaluations of the Customs Act 2023, import duty waivers, the Authorised Economic Operator programme and the National Single Window. “A reform that is never evaluated cannot be improved, and I would sooner hear hard truths from Ibadan than discover them too late in the field,” he said. Adeniyi said Customs remained central to protecting Nigeria’s revenue, securing its borders and facilitating legitimate trade. “The world is not borderless. It is connected, and that connection makes the border more important, not less,” he said. Earlier, the Director of the TETFund Centre of Excellence in Security Management, Professor Benjamin Aluko, said the Centre was ready to support Customs through research, professional education and interdisciplinary collaboration. He disclosed that the Centre’s master’s programme in Security Management began in the 2024/2025 academic session with approximately 40 students, largely from security agencies, including Customs. Its doctoral programme is expected to admit its first cohort in the next academic session. The director said the Centre was developing a curriculum for senior Customs officers with support from the Institute for Peace and Strategic Studies and specialists in economics, accounting, sociology, business administration, psychology and other disciplines. He appealed to Adeniyi to provide a 30-seater bus for student field trips and support the establishment of a research and training facility proposed to be named the Bashir Adewale Adeniyi Research and Training Hub. “Our mandate is to strengthen security management through research, professional training and the development of effective early-warning systems.” “We believe that collaboration between academia and security agencies is essential to developing practical solutions to Nigeria’s security challenges.” “The proposed Customs training curriculum will equip senior officers with multidisciplinary knowledge to address emerging security threats.” “Our master’s programme has commenced, and we look forward to launching the PhD programme in the next academic session.” “We appeal for support to acquire a 30-seater Coaster bus to facilitate students’ field research and practical learning.” “A dedicated research and training hub will strengthen our capacity to conduct research and provide specialised training for security professionals,” he said. The Executive Secretary of TETFund, Sonny Echono, was represented at the event by the Director of Research and Development/Centres of Excellence Development, Suleiman Zangina.
