items.title: Ghana’s economic recovery: Distinguishing policy continuity from political propaganda
items.description: If the IMF commends Ghana for its economic recovery, such recognition should not automatically be interpreted as praise for the NDC government alone. The 36-month Extended Credit Facility (ECF) programme was approved in May 2023, under the previous administration. By October 2023, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva had already acknowledged Ghana’s recovery efforts, including progress in addressing the country’s debt challenges. International credit rating agencies have also recognised the contribution of debt restructuring to Ghana’s economic stabilisation efforts. The following assessments provide important evidence for understanding the origins and evolution of Ghana’s economic recovery. 1. IMF: Debt Restructuring and Macroeconomic Stabilisation In its 10 December 2024 Third Review of Ghana’s Extended Credit Facility (ECF) programme, the IMF reported that economic growth was recovering faster than expected, inflation was declining, and the country’s fiscal and external positions had improved considerably. The Fund also highlighted progress in domestic debt restructuring, the agreement with official creditors, and the successful Eurobond exchange. These developments demonstrate that significant elements of Ghana’s economic recovery were already underway before the change of government in January 2025. 2. S&P Global Ratings: Debt Restructuring and Fiscal Space In its 14 October 2024 assessment, S&P Global Ratings explained that Ghana’s restructuring of US$13.1 billion in Eurobonds was intended to ease external debt-servicing pressures and restore public debt sustainability. The agency estimated that the restructuring, combined with the earlier Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP), would reduce interest expenditure to below 20% of government revenue in 2025, compared with more than 47% in 2022. It also estimated that the Eurobond restructuring would provide approximately US$4.4 billion in cash-flow relief over the lifespan of the IMF programme. This relief was expected to ease the government’s financing constraints, reduce debt-servicing pressures, and create fiscal space for economic stabilisation. Consequently, debt restructuring constituted an important component of the recovery process initiated before the current administration assumed office. 3. IMF: The Continuity of the Economic Recovery Programme In its June 2025 Fourth Review, the IMF reiterated the importance of Ghana’s comprehensive debt restructuring in restoring debt sustainability. The programme sought to reduce the present value of public debt relative to GDP and lower the external debt-service-to-revenue ratio. The Fund also reported that Ghana’s real GDP growth had increased from 3.1% in 2023 to 5.7% in 2024, although favourable international gold prices and other factors also contributed to the improved performance. The IMF’s assessment supports the conclusion that debt restructuring was a SIGNIFICANT component of the broader policy framework underpinning Ghana’s economic recovery. The recovery, THEREFORE, should not be attributed exclusively to the new administration. That assertion is completely misleading! INDEED, THE NEW ADMINISTRATION DIDN’T BRING ON BOARD ANYTHING EXTRAORDINARY! IT ONLY CAME TO CONTINUE WHAT WAS ALREADY BEING DONE! 4. Fitch Ratings: Debt Restructuring and Improved Creditworthiness In June 2025, Fitch upgraded Ghana’s long-term foreign-currency issuer default rating from Restricted Default to B− with a Stable Outlook. The upgrade reflected progress in debt restructuring, fiscal consolidation, and an improving macroeconomic outlook. This rating action provides further evidence that Ghana’s debt restructuring and broader macroeconomic adjustments contributed to an improvement in the country’s credit standing. Although the upgrade occurred under the current administration, the restructuring process and several associated policy measures had commenced under the previous government. The timing of the upgrade must therefore be distinguished from the period in which the underlying reforms were initiated and implemented. THE EVIDENCE FROM THE IMF AND THE INTERNATIONAL CREDIT RATING AGENCIES CLEARLY INDICATES THAT GHANA’S ECONOMIC RECOVERY WAS ALREADY UNDERWAY BEFORE THE CHANGE OF GOVERNMENT IN JANUARY 2025. The current administration inherited an ongoing IMF-supported programme that had been implemented for approximately 19 months, with measurable progress already recorded. Its contribution should therefore be evaluated within the broader context of policy continuity, while recognising that external developments may also have influenced certain economic outcomes. The political propaganda surrounding Ghana’s economic recovery is excessive! Economic analysis must distinguish between initiating a policy programme, implementing its principal reforms, and continuing an existing programme. A balanced assessment should acknowledge the contributions of both administrations and recognise the role of the IMF-supported programme in the recovery process.

items.title: The future of rule: More questions than answers
items.description: It took four days of successive presidential reiterations before the various parties began to grasp that, this time, it is different. And no wonder. Never in Egypt’s modern history has the head of state chosen to hand power over voluntarily. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi himself promised , time and again, during his first term that he would not move to amend the constitution and extend his rule. That changed at the start of his second term, when the constitution was in fact amended, and he secured two further terms, keeping him in office until 2030. That’s why when the president opened his speech at the Armed Forces’ educational seminar on Wednesday by announcing he would not extend his rule, the confusion was plain on all sides, state institutions included. At the seminar, Sisi said he had no intention of amending the Constitution. The audience hesitated for a few seconds before applauding. And many people noticed . The next day, he stated the announcement in clearer terms. But the statement, issued by the presidential spokesperson, was edited, changing “until 2030” into “until the last day of his rule.” There is a big difference between the two formulations. The latter preserves a measure of vagueness, which some apparently felt was needed until things became clearer. Sisi alluded to this confusion on Saturday, at the Egyptian Military Academy’s first cohort graduation ceremony, when he spoke of wishes relayed by pro-government media figures to delay announcing his decision for the sake of “the state.” But according to Sisi’s speech, broadcast on live television, what “the state” actually needs is an early announcement that opens the door to a continuing journey to prepare “a replacement.” And so, without any equivocation, Sisi announced his decision to leave office in 2030. And at the same time, he sketched the contours of a roadmap for the transfer of power and of the role he expects to play during this period and, perhaps, even after power passes to a new president. Mada Masr spoke to sources who all point to the widespread state of confusion brought about by the president’s announcement, but they also say that what he is proposing amounts to a radical change in the form and nature of rule in Egypt, one the country may have never seen before. Three informed sources agree that the president is managing the details of his exit from power with a “very narrow circle that sits outside the [state] agencies.” A political source close to one of the sovereign agencies says the vagueness created by Sisi’s first two announcements led some people affiliated with state entities or institutions to volunteer initiatives expressing their rejection of the president leaving power, as a precaution, “for fear of appearing to go along with the matter of his departure,” in the absence of security guidance. Those attempts stopped completely after the latest announcement, he adds. The lack of guidance, according to the source, stemmed from the fact that Sisi’s announcement caught the leaders of the various sovereign agencies off guard. They were hearing the details of his roadmap for the first time, he says. That surprise pushed the different agencies to hold emergency meetings that same evening to discuss the announcement, the source adds. A second politician close to one of the sovereign agencies points to a state of confusion and worry within the security apparatus, which now faces a new reality with no plan on how to deal with it, given the absence of any coordination between the presidency and the agencies before the announcement. One reason for that worry, according to the first source, is the fear that society would take these statements as a sign of greater political openness and more room for opposition. The agencies would then be left with resolving that situation, either on their own or after receiving orders from above, the source says. As a senior government official speaking to Mada Masr puts it, “the heads of the agencies can’t figure [Sisi] out or know what he wants.” But confusion aside, all parties now face a new reality of which only sparse details are clear: how Sisi envisions managing this transitional phase and guaranteeing the handover. In his Saturday speech, Sisi pointed to Article 200 of the Constitution , which sets out the Armed Forces’ duties. Since the 2019 amendments, those duties include “uphold[ing] the Constitution and democracy” and “preserv[ing] the key tenets and the civilian nature of the State.” According to the president, this is the constitutional article on which his roadmap rests. He made sure to read the text of the article out — but not all of it. He noted only that its last sentence “talks about how there have to be laws regulating what I’ve mentioned.” Not exactly. The final sentence only states that “The Armed Forces shall have a supreme council as regulated by Law.” It makes no mention of any law governing the military’s role in “uphold[ing] the Constitution and democracy.” Somehow, Sisi is leaning on that sentence to justify the starting point of his plan: a new law, drafted under the supervision of a new committee. As the president described it, the committee would be chaired by the House of Representatives’ speaker, with the higher education and justice ministers as members, along with a number of thinkers and politicians. Its mandate is specific: to debate the law and draft a proposal. Issam Islamboly, a Supreme Constitutional Court lawyer, tells Mada Masr that the proposal Sisi outlined on Saturday could amount to “new restrictions” on the conditions for running for president, one that conflicts with the Constitution’s provisions. Sisi hinted at requirements such as holding a PhD or completing a 30-month program at the Military Academy. To Islamboly, this is an “expansive” interpretation of Article 200, which adds the safeguarding of democracy to the Armed Forces’ duties. “Protecting democracy doesn’t come through laws on presidential elections,” he says. The presidential directive to the proposed committee spells out what it should develop: a 30-month study and training program at the Military Academy for prospective presidential candidates. According to Sisi, then, the part the Military Academy is expected to play will be the mechanism that defines what the Armed Forces’ role in “uphold[ing] the Constitution and democracy” will look like in the coming years. One of the political sources points to unease in some circles close to the regime over the Military Academy’s growing role. Over the past years, the source explains, it has displaced the National Training Academy, which was founded in 2017 to develop young cadres and which reports to the presidency. In recent years, undergoing and passing Military Academy training has become a prerequisite for any state appointment, from imams and teachers to judges . But even with that expansion, taking charge of qualifying candidates for the presidency is a whole other level. The first political source says the prevailing impression is that the academy’s role in a candidate qualification program is nothing more than a “formality,” since it is established that any future president must have the Supreme Council of the Armed Forces’ approval. That makes passing the academy’s training a marginal matter, whether the candidate comes from a military background or is a civilian, he adds. It is unclear whether this role will end once power has passed from Sisi to a new president. Does the committee’s work stop once the candidates are chosen, or is there some sort of oversight role afterward? Will there be some kind of supreme council down the line with supervisory authority over the next president? The three informed sources point to the “Turkish” model as they try to imagine the nature of the arrangements that might follow the transfer of power and how the constitutional text appointing the Armed Forces as guardians of the Constitution and democracy could be translated in practice. Since the 1920s, the Turkish armed forces have assigned themselves the guardian responsible for protecting the secular republic. And indeed, they have intervened repeatedly, including with the ousting of Necmettin Erbakan, the Islamist-leaning prime minister who was forced to resign on the grounds that he had violated the values of the secular state. In 2016, factions within the Turkish military tried to overthrow the current president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, but the attempt failed. Building such an arrangement for the Egyptian Armed Forces would take far more than a legal amendment. It would mean changing the nature and form of rule in Egypt, moving from a direct presidential model to one in which heads of state answer to some form of authority above them, something that would most likely require a constitutional amendment. In all cases, the sources agree that the current proposal represents a massive shift in the nature of rule in Egypt, unlike any formula the country has seen before. But that, they say, opens the door to different possibilities. As a start, “people’s consciousness has taken in that there is a life after Sisi,” as political researcher Amr Abdel Rahman puts it. For Akram Ismail, the Civil Democratic Movement general coordinator, “there will be room for choice and room for competition between wings of the regime that, to settle it, would have to call in the people.” This calling on the public could allow for some “loosening up” that could “open up a space for us,” he tells Mada Masr. The post The future of rule: More questions than answers first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: ECG to begin nationwide meter audit to curb electricity theft
items.description: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) is set to commence a nationwide meter audit exercise across all its operational areas to reduce commercial losses, improve revenue assurance and combat electricity theft. In a statement, ECG said the exercise would involve inspecting and verifying prepaid and postpaid meters, Special Load Tariff (SLT) installations and associated wiring “to confirm the integrity of metering systems and ensure accurate measurement and billing of electricity consumption.” The company said the announcement served as official notice of the exercise, stressing that “no further prior notices, appointment letters, or advance notifications will be issued.” It therefore urged customers, landlords, estate managers, property managers, facility managers and security personnel not to deny or delay access to authorised ECG personnel on the grounds that they had not received a separate notification letter. ECG cited Regulation 4(h) of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (Customer Service) Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2413), which requires consumers to grant utility employees or authorised agents safe and reasonable access to their premises, subject to the production of verifiable identification and compliance with the utility’s customer charter. “All ECG employees and authorised agents participating in the exercise will carry official ECG identification cards,” the statement said, urging customers to verify the identities of field personnel before granting them access.

items.title: Le maire de Tevrag, Zeina : « le programme de développement de Nouakchott a eu des répercussions positives sur les citoyens »
items.description: Le maire de Tevrag Zeina, Taleb Abderrahmane El Mahjoub, a déclaré que les récentes visites de terrain menées par les autorités avaient mis en évidence l'ampleur des réalisations accomplies dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du programme de développement de la ville de Nouakchott, ainsi que les services directs qu'elles offrent désormais aux citoyens. Le maire a ajouté, dans un communiqué publié ce mardi, que les visites effectuées par le Premier ministre Mokhtar Diay, accompagné d’un certain nombre de ministres et de responsables concernés, ont permis de se rendre compte de près d’un certain nombre d’ouvrages et d’équipements publics désormais opérationnels, dans les domaines de l’eau, de la santé, de l’éducation, des routes et des infrastructures. Il a précisé que les sites visités dans sa commune reflétaient, selon son observation, le degré de satisfaction des usagers vis-à-vis des projets réalisés, soulignant la satisfaction des habitants quant aux services fournis et à l’impact de ces réalisations sur leur vie quotidienne. Le maire de Tevrag Zeina a salué les réalisations accomplies dans le cadre du programme de développement de la ville de Nouakchott et des autres programmes et interventions gouvernementales, estimant qu’elles ont contribué à améliorer la qualité des services fournis aux citoyens et à renforcer leur accès aux équipements publics. À cette occasion, le maire a appelé à poursuivre la mise en œuvre des programmes de développement et à redoubler d’efforts pour réaliser davantage de transformations dans divers domaines.

items.title: Décès de l’actrice tunisienne Amel Baccouche
items.description: C’est avec une grande tristesse que nous avons appris, ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, le décès de l’actrice tunisienne Amel Baccouche, à l’âge de 77 ans. La défunte a interprété de nombreux rôles, notamment celui de «Jannette» dans la série populaire Choufli Hall , aux côtés de Kamel Touati, Mouna Noureddine, le regretté Sofiène Chaari, Jamila Chihi et Kaouther Belhaj. Cette dernière avait d’ailleurs rendu visite à la grande artiste Amel Baccouche, en septembre dernier, à son domicile, afin de prendre de ses nouvelles après un récent problème de santé. Elle était en convalescence et se reposait auprès de sa famille. Toutefois, son état de santé s’est de nouveau détérioré ces derniers jours… Amel Baccouche a commencé sa carrière d’actrice dans les années 1970 au sein de la Troupe permanente du Kef sous la direction de feu Moncef Souissi et de Kamel Allaoui, qui fut son premier époux. items.title: Meet Nigeria’s youngest female SAN, Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle
items.description: Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle has made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), attaining the prestigious legal rank at the age of 40. She was among 68 legal practitioners sworn in as Senior Advocates of Nigeria by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on October 12, 2026, during the opening of the 2026/2027 legal year. Four women were among the newly elevated practitioners. Born on June 25, 1986, in Kaduna State, Ehinfun-Adekunle hails from Ijero-Ekiti in Ekiti State. Her journey into the legal profession began with her studies at Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, where she obtained her Bachelor of Laws degree between 2003 and 2009. She proceeded to the Nigerian Law School, where she studied from 2009 to 2010, before earning a Master of Laws degree in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom, between 2011 and 2012. She is also a member of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators in the UK. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. in September 2013, Ehinfun-Adekunle worked at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. She subsequently became a partner at Afe Babalola & Co., where her areas of practice include complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, oil and gas, arbitration, election petitions, transactional law and regulatory compliance. Her professional experience has also included appearances before the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court of Nigeria. The Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee approved her elevation to the rank of SAN on July 23, 2026, before she was formally sworn in alongside 67 other legal practitioners in October. Ehinfun-Adekunle’s interest in law reportedly developed during her childhood. Her parents described her as talkative, a trait also reflected in her primary school reports. Stories told by her father about politics in the old Western Region and the legal career of Chief Rotimi Williams, popularly known as “Timi the Law”, helped shape her interest in the profession. Several prominent figures have influenced her career, including Aare Afe Babalola, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, Kehinde Ogunwumiju and Pastor R. A. Ogunwole. Beyond her legal practice, Ehinfun-Adekunle has spoken about the challenges confronting Nigeria’s justice system, particularly delays in the administration of justice and the financial burden prolonged litigation places on individuals and businesses. The post Meet Nigeria’s youngest female SAN, Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: I’ll pursue all lawful avenues to clear my name – Embattled Obuasi SHTS headmaster
items.description: The headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, says he will devote his attention and resources to clearing his name following allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at the school. Mr Abdulai said this as he resigned as Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Juaben Constituency and withdrew his candidature for the constituency chairmanship. In an October 20 letter to the NDC General Secretary, he said his resignation and withdrawal from the forthcoming constituency elections took immediate effect. “At this time, I intend to devote my attention and resources to pursuing all lawful avenues to clear my name and vindicate my position. I remain hopeful that, once these matters are resolved, I will be able to return to active political engagement and continue contributing to the ideals and aspirations of the NDC,” he stated. The decision comes amid public concern over allegations that Mr Abdulai sexually abused more than 14 female students at the school. The allegations have triggered calls for accountability and a thorough investigation. Mr Abdulai maintained his innocence and expressed gratitude to friends, relatives and supporters who have continued to believe in him. “I wish to express my profound gratitude to my friends, relatives, and all well-wishers who have stood by me and maintained their faith in my innocence in the face of the allegations levelled against me and my office,” he said. He also thanked the NDC for giving him the opportunity to serve the party and contribute to its growth and development. Read also: Obuasi SHTS headmaster resigns as NDC constituency secretary, withdraws from chairmanship race Mr Abdulai did not provide details of the legal steps he intends to pursue or indicate when he expects the matter to be resolved. His letter was copied to the NDC National Chairman and the party’s Ashanti Regional Chairman. The allegations have also prompted the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) to call for the removal of the headmaster and Ghana Education Service (GES) officials in Obuasi over their alleged handling of complaints concerning the case. NAGRAT President Jacob Anaba has claimed that concerns about the alleged misconduct were raised before the matter became public and questioned whether the relevant education authorities responded appropriately. The allegations remain subject to investigation.

items.title: Souveraineté numérique et emploi : Ahmed Rahhou promet un écosystème intégré
items.description: Lors de la cérémonie de passation des pouvoirs qui s'est déroulée ce lundi 19 octobre 2026 à Rabat avec Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, Ahmed Rahhou, que le Roi Mohammed VI a nommé ministre de l'Intelligence artificielle, de la Transformation numérique et de la Réforme de l'administration, a formulé l'engagement fort d'ériger le chantier de la digitalisation et de l'intelligence artificielle en un véritable écosystème économique intégré, générateur de valeur ajoutée et créateur d’emplois pour la jeunesse. S'exprimant à cette occasion en présence de Aïcha Guellaa, ministre déléguée chargée de la Réforme de l'administration, le nouveau ministre a précisé que la réalisation de cette promesse stratégique repose sur la mise en place d'un environnement propice au développement des start-ups et à l'attraction des investissements, couplé à la qualification des ressources humaines nationales, à la sécurisation des infrastructures et à la maîtrise des coûts énergétiques. Ahmed Rahhou a de même souligné que l'IA et la digitalisation constituent un double levier : d'une part, un outil d'optimisation du service public et de lutte contre la corruption, et d'autre part, un moteur de croissance économique autonome. Il a affirmé que son département adoptera une démarche transversale et participative pour relever les défis majeurs de la souveraineté numérique, de la cybersécurité et de la protection des données. Pour sa part, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni a rappelé les jalons posés sous sa gouvernance, notamment la stratégie « Maroc Digital 2030 » , l'organisation des assises nationales sur l'IA et l'élaboration de la feuille de route visant à faire du Royaume un producteur de technologies plutôt qu'un simple consommateur. De son côté, Aïcha Guellaa a réaffirmé son engagement à faire de la modernisation de l'appareil administratif un catalyseur pour l'investissement et l'insertion professionnelle des jeunes. items.title: At SCO, Dar calls for promoting use of national currencies to help offset global economic shocks
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday encouraged members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to use national currencies for “mutual settlement” and establish other financial mechanisms to “offset international financial shocks”. He made the remarks while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting in Tajikistan’s capital Dushanbe, where he arrived a day earlier. The SCO comprises 10 member states, namely Pakistan, China, India, Iran, Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The two observer states are Afghanistan and Mongolia. The CHG is the SCO’s second-highest decision-making body and provides guidance on economic, financial, trade, connectivity and socio-economic cooperation, as well as the organisation’s budgetary matters. Addressing the SCO meeting, Dar highlighted the “need to accelerate efforts to promote the use of national currencies for mutual settlement”, as well as to establish the SCO Development Bank, SCO Development Fund and SCO Investment Fund. “Such tools are measures which will advance development initiatives and help the SCO region to offset international financial shocks,” the former finance minister noted. Dar reiterated his call to accelerate local currency settlements in a later address to an expanded-format session of the meeting. Two members of the SCO, Russia and Iran, face Western sanctions restricting their access to international markets and stifling their economic growth. In the joint communiqué for the Pakistan-chaired 2024 CHG meeting , SCO member states had reaffirmed the need for consistent implementation of a roadmap on gradual increase in the share of national currencies in mutual settlements. It underlined the need to protect and promote the World Trade Organisation’s multilateral trade system for inclusive global growth and reduce reliance on the American currency for international trade transactions. At that summit, PM Shehbaz Sharif had noted “growing consensus among the member states on the use of mutual currencies for settlements” and said such a transition would “shield us from global financial disruptions”. Speaking in Dushanbe, Dar highlighted that the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) offered “every SCO partner a compelling opportunity to participate in and accelerate our shared journey towards comprehensive economic integration”. “For our region to achieve seamless economic integration, targeted investment in core sectors, most notably in energy and transport, is vital,” he stressed. The foreign minister criticised “protectionist policies and unilateral coercive measures”, saying they contradicted the principles of international law, “suppress economic growth, block technological progress and increase inequality”. “Therefore, reform of the global financial architecture and trade regimes is essential for achieving equitable global development,” the deputy PM declared. He said Pakistan strongly advocated for “expanding investments into high-potential industries, including agriculture, mining and minerals, and information technology, to build a resilient and interconnected economic future”. He expressed Pakistan’s “belief that artificial intelligence, digital transformation, innovation, energy cooperation and international information security should become important pillars of future cooperation within the SCO”. Dar then recalled the priority areas identified by PM Shehbaz for the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) summit that Islamabad is set to host in 2027. These comprised peace, security and mutual trust; regional connectivity and trade; innovation, AI and digital transformation; climate resilience and sustainable energy; and people-to-people exchanges. He emphasised that strategic investment in transport and energy infrastructure was not merely beneficial but “absolutely imperative for true regional economic integration”. At the outset of his speech, Dar extended his appreciation to the Tajik government and people for their “very warm and generous hospitality”. “For the past 25 years, the SCO has remained anchored in the Shanghai spirit of mutual trust and respect for diversity and expanded its mandate to encompass trade, infrastructure, culture and innovation,” he noted. Dar went on to state that Pakistan’s journey within the SCO highlighted its commitment to the Shanghai spirit, recalling that the country’s chairmanship of SCO’s Reg­ional Anti-Terrorist Structure (SCO-RATS) and the SCO Working Group on Poverty Alleviation. He said Pakistan intended to highlight the role of small and medium enterprises in reducing poverty. ‘Pakistan wants peaceful, regionally integrated Afghanistan’ During his speech at the CHG summit, DPM Dar also raised the issue of cross-border terrorism emanating from Afghanistan. Noting that sustainable economic development cannot be guaranteed without durable peace and security in the region, he said ensuring stability in Afghanistan was “imperative” for safeguarding regional peace. “Pakistan continues to be desirous of a peaceful, stable, regionally integrated and prosperous Afghanistan, which is at peace with itself and its neighbours.” The deputy premier pointed out that Islamabad had only one expectation from the “Afghan Taliban regime: that Afghan territory should not be used for terrorism against Pakistan and the world”. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to a peaceful and stable neighbourhood as an essential foundation for regional development and prosperity. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Concluding his address, Dar congratulated Tajikistan and the heads of SCO’s permanent bodies on the successful completion of the CHG meeting, and congratulated Uzbekistan for taking over the chair. He also commended the SCO national coordinators for their help in finalising documents. He stated: “The fundamental strength of the SCO is anchored not only in our deeply intertwined histories, but more importantly, in the resilient, shared future that we collectively choose to forge. “Pakistan stands resolute in its commitment to serve as an active architect of this shared destiny, and to shape the next decade of Eurasian connectivity and economic prosperity.” Recommendations to deepen intra-SCO cooperation Addressing an expanded-format session of the CHG meeting later, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to regional harmony, trade, transit connectivity and economic integration as “a natural bridge connecting South Asia, Central Asia, and Eurasia”. “Pakistan firmly believes that dialogue and diplomacy offer the most effective path to resolving regional tensions,” he said, highlighting the country’s efforts for de-escalation in the Middle East. To this effect, Pakistan remains engaged in mediation efforts between the US and Iran, he added. “We will continue to support all efforts for dialogue and peaceful resolution of disputes for lasting peace and stability,” the foreign minister said. “Our diplomatic strategy is guided by our firm belief that regional challenges require collective, cooperative, and sustainable multilateral solutions.” He went on to highlight that SCO had transformed from a regional confidence-building platform into a premier transcontinental organisation representing over 40 per cent of humanity. Dar further highlighted that the intra-SCO trade had expanded significantly, proving that cooperative multilateralism can effectively drive stability and sustainable development across our shared continent. “The future prospects of the SCO remain bright,” the deputy premier remarked, noting that the region was situated at the crossroads of major international trade corridors. By leveraging our vast natural resources, technological advancements, and vibrant human capital, the SCO could lead digital transformation, industrial growth, and sustainable economic development across Eurasia, he emphasised. To realise this vision, the foreign minister also proposed recommendations to deepen economic cooperation among SCO countries and expand international partnerships. Firstly, Dar called for empowering the SCO Chambers of Commerce and Business Council by establishing direct business-to-business links and organising joint trade expos. He also urged member states to streamline customs procedures to support SMEs. Secondly, he proposed the strengthening of the SCO Interbank Consortium (IBC). “We must accelerate local currency settlements and enhance the SCO Interbank Consortium framework to mitigate external financial risks, harmonise cross-border payment systems, and facilitate seamless trade financing,” he said. Pending the establishment of the SCO Development Bank, the IBC can play a more active role in financing infrastructure upgrades, Dar added. He underlined that Habib Bank Limited (HBL), the current chair of the IBC, can help advance this agenda through close coordination with fellow members. At last, the foreign minister recommended expanding international partnerships. “The SCO should actively expand structured partnerships with international organisations including the United Nations, Asean, the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO), and other international and regional financial institutions, to reinforce an open, rules-based, and inclusive regional order,” Dar underscored. He added: “Pakistan recommends that the SCO adopt a forward-looking strategy focused on joint technological innovation, climate resilience, energy security and secure supply chains. “We must also operationalise Eurasian energy and transport corridors while deepening people-to-people ties, cultural exchanges, and educational partnerships.” Concluding his speech, Dar said Pakistan looked forward to welcoming the heads of state at the SCO CHS summit in Islamabad in August 2027. “Pakistan remains steadfast in its resolve to foster a peaceful, interconnected, and prosperous SCO community. Together, let us forge a shared future of enduring prosperity for all our people,” he resolved. Dar meets Tajik FM Later in the day, Dar met with Tajikistan’s FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin on the sidelines of the meeting. The two ministers “reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly ties between Pakistan and Tajikistan, rooted in shared history, culture and faith”, the Foreign Office (FO) said. They underscored the need to further expand trade and economic cooperation, enhance regional connectivity and strengthen cooperation in energy, security and people-to-people exchanges. The foreign ministers also exchanged views on regional and global developments and underscored the importance of continued coordination at regional and multilateral forums to advance shared goals of peace and prosperity, FO added. Ahead of the SCO meeting, DPM Dar called on Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, along with other heads of delegations. “President Rahmon welcomed the leaders and emphasised the importance of strengthening regional economic cooperation under the SCO to promote connectivity, stability and shared prosperity,” FO said. He, along with other delegates, was then welcomed by PM Qohir Rasulzoda. During his visit, Dar will also hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the SCO moot, according to FO. On Monday , Dar held a meeting with the Tajik premier. He also met with China’s PM Li Qiang and Mongolia’s First DPM Jadambyn Enkhbayar on the sidelines of a banquet dinner hosted for the delegates. Pakistan, which hosted a CHG meeting in October 2024, is now scheduled to host the CHS summit in 2027 after it assumed the chairmanship last month. On Sept 30, Dar reviewed preparations for the CHS summit as SCO national coordinators , who were in Islamabad for a meeting, called on him. In July, Pakistan hosted the 12th meeting of the Heads of Border Services of the Competent Authorities of the SCO.

items.title: ​Mairie de Dixinn : « Neuf mois sans salaire : trop, c’est trop ! », les travailleurs menacent de déclencher une grève générale
items.description: ​Le torchon brûle entre les autorités communales de Dixinn et leurs employés. Ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, lors d'une déclaration conjointe lue par Kalifa DIAWARA, secrétaire général de la section syndicale CNTG, aux côtés de la COSATREG, les travailleurs ont fermement dénoncé leurs conditions de vie et posé un ultimatum aux autorités communales. Faute d'accord satisfaisant sur leurs arriérés de salaires, une grève générale illimitée est annoncée à compter du lundi 26 octobre 2026 à 08 heures. ​« Le moment est grave » ​D'entrée de jeu, les centrales syndicales CNTG et COSATREG ont tenu à planter le décor d'une crise qui dure depuis le début de l'année : « Le moment est grave : des femmes et des hommes qui servent la Commune de Dixinn depuis des années travaillent sans être payés » , a déploré Kalifa DIAWARA, secrétaire général de la section syndicale CNTG et syndicat des travailleurs de la commune de Dixinn. ​Bien que des négociations se soient ouvertes récemment, la proposition des autorités d'apurer uniquement les reliquats de l'exercice précédent tout en ignorant l'année en cours a irrité les représentants des salariés : ​ « Le dialogue s'est ouvert le 19 octobre, mais la proposition qui nous a été faite, payer seulement les deux mois de 2025 et ne plus parler des salaires de 2026, est inacceptable. Les contractuels ont travaillé, et contribué à mobiliser les ressources propres de la Commune, depuis le 1er janvier 2026. Et si rien ne change, la grève générale illimitée débutera le lundi 26 octobre 2026 à 08 heures » , a-t-il martelé. ​Des agents dévoués mais « considérés comme licenciés » sans indemnisation ​Le syndicat dénonce une situation précaire frappant des travailleurs parfois en poste depuis plusieurs décennies, alors même qu'ils continuent d'assurer le fonctionnement des services municipaux et le recouvrement des recettes : ​« Les agents contractuels de la Commune de Dixinn sont employés depuis plus de dix (10) ans, certains depuis plus de vingt (20) ans. Depuis le 1er janvier 2026, ils n'ont perçu aucun salaire, après deux (2) mois d'impayés en 2025. Les primes de fonction des chefs de service sont impayées depuis la même date. Et l'on prétend les considérer comme licenciés, en s'appuyant sur une décision de résiliation du président de la Délégation Spéciale, sans procédure ni indemnisation » , déplore-t-il. Avant d'ajouter : « Malgré l'absence de salaire, ces agents n'ont pas cessé de travailler. Ils ont continué d'assurer l'état civil, le recouvrement des impôts et taxes et les autres services générateurs de recettes […]. Cette contribution doit être reconnue : il plaide pour le paiement de leurs salaires, et non pour leur licenciement. » ​Refus du « silence sur 2026 » ​Face à la proposition de la mairie de restreindre le règlement des arriérés à l'exercice 2025, la réponse syndicale est sans équivoque : « Madame le Maire veut payer les deux mois de 2025 et demande que l'on ne parle plus des salaires de 2026. Nous la rejetons, pour trois raisons. » ​« Elle efface neuf mois de travail : ce travail a été fourni, il doit être payé. Un salaire dû ne disparaît pas parce que l’employeur préfère ne plus en parler. « Elle est contraire à la loi : la rémunération est une charge obligatoire du budget communal, l'action en paiement n'est pas prescrite, et aucun travailleur ne peut être contraint d'abandonner ses salaires. ​« Elle ne règle rien : payer 2025 est un premier pas, jamais une solution. Il ne peut pas se faire au prix du silence sur 2026. » ​Déterminés à faire valoir leurs droits, les syndicats préviennent qu'ils iront au bout de leur démarche si aucun compromis n'est trouvé avant la date butoir : ​ « Nous ne voulons pas de cette grève, mais nous irons jusqu'au bout. Si ces revendications ne sont pas satisfaites, les travailleuses et travailleurs de la Commune de Dixinn entreront en grève générale illimitée à compter du lundi 26 octobre 2026 à 08 heures, jusqu'à satisfaction. » Les syndicats appellent les agents à rester mobilisés et disciplinés, tout en présentant leurs excuses à la population pour les éventuelles perturbations des services communaux. Interrogée par la presse, Madame le maire n’a pas souhaité commenter cette situation.

items.title: AIK chief scout Herish Sadi arrives in Accra for One World Sports Management’s West Africa Talent Hunt tournament
items.description: The chief football scout at Swedish football side AIK, Herish Sadi, has arrived in Accra for the West Africa Ralent Hunt tournament. Sadi arrives in Ghana for the three-day football tournament put together by One World Sports Management to unearth talent from the western side of the continent. The 37-year-old was the scout behind the discovery of Brighton and Hove Albion forward Zadok Yohanna, taking him from Nigeria to AIK in Sweden. The idea behind Sadi’s arrival in Ghana is to watch and identify talented players who are capable of making the jump from Africa to Europe, with the scout working together with the administrators of One World Sports Management. Speaking following his arrival in Ghana, Sadi asked young players to always be ready for the next step, as there are several opportunities. “You need to always be on your toes because you never know when it’s going to happen; people’s lives change overnight,” he said. “You need to be sharp, be on your toes to do your bets all the time, and hopefully that is enough for somebody to recognise you and make the change that you want. “You need to relax, enjoy the game, be proud and fight for what you want.” Six teams are involved in this year’s West Africa Talent Hunt tournament, including Great Somas, Nice Ibrahim, Visio FC, Liberty Academy, Exulted FC and Sakibatti. The final day of the tournament is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21.

items.title: GES directs Ashanti Regional and Obuasi Municipal education directors to step aside over Obuasi SHTS probe
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has directed the Ashanti Regional Director of Education, Dr William Amankrah Appiah, and the Obuasi Municipal Director of Education, Kwamena Owusu-Nketiah, to step aside with immediate effect as investigations continue into allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and signed by its Head of Public Relations, Daniel Fenyi, the GES said the directive was intended to ensure the investigation proceeds without interference or the perception of interference. The two directors have been instructed to hand over their offices and all state property in their possession to the Deputy Ashanti Regional Director of Education, Thomas Kwame Boateng. The GES also reaffirmed that Mr Abdulai remains interdicted, dismissing reports circulating that he had been cleared. “The public is urged to ignore any news making the rounds that the headmaster has been cleared,” the statement said. Management of the Service called for calm, support and cooperation as investigations into the matter continue. The directive follows mounting pressure from civil society organisations, including RISE-Ghana, over the handling of the allegations against Mr Abdulai. The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has also directed Mr Abdulai to step aside from the Juaben Constituency Chairmanship race pending the outcome of an investigation by the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service. A JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni reported that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports concerning alleged sexual abuse by the headmaster months before his suspension. The number of students alleging abuse has reportedly risen to 16. The Education Ministry has directed the CID to investigate the allegations. The decision to have the two education directors step aside comes as authorities face calls to establish how the allegations were handled and ensure the investigation proceeds without interference. The GES has urged stakeholders to cooperate with the process as investigators work to establish the facts. The allegations against Mr Abdulai have not been established, and he remains entitled to the presumption of innocence.

items.title: Eniola Badmus apologises to Laide Bakare, calls for end to feud
items.description: Nollywood actress Eniola Badmus has apologised to her colleague, Laide Bakare, following the backlash over her reaction to Bakare’s name during a recent podcast appearance, expressing a desire to put their differences behind them. Badmus tendered the apology in a statement shared on Instagram on Tuesday, days after a clip from her appearance on Isbae U’s Curiosity Made Me Ask podcast went viral on social media. During the interview, the host mentioned Bakare as one of his favourite actresses, prompting Badmus to hiss and change her facial expression. The moment attracted reactions online and revived discussions about the strained relationship between the two actresses. Reflecting on her reaction via her Instagram page, Badmus admitted that it could have been perceived as dismissive and expressed regret over how it came across. “On reflection, I realise my reaction when Laide Bakare’s name was mentioned during my recent interview could have come across as dismissive, and for that, I sincerely apologise,” she wrote. Addressing Bakare directly, the actress added, “Laide, whatever our differences, I choose peace and I genuinely wish you well.” Badmus said maturity involves learning from past experiences and choosing to move forward rather than holding on to disagreements. “We’re all growing, learning and becoming better versions of ourselves. Sometimes maturity is simply knowing when to let go and move forward,” she stated. She concluded her message with a plea for peace, writing, “Joo maa binu. No negativity. No grudges. Let love lead and peace reigns.” The apology comes amid a history of public disagreements between the actresses, whose relationship has been marked by exchanges on social media and confrontations at public events. In March 2024, Badmus appeared to mock Bakare’s outfit at the latter’s book launch. Bakare had attended the event in a white outfit with an orange cape, which generated mixed reactions online. Badmus subsequently took to Instagram and wrote, “Ewo ninu yin lo wo Aso Pastor Ajidara. Abeg who??” The remark was widely interpreted as a dig at Bakare’s outfit. Bakare expressed disappointment over the incident, questioning why a colleague she regarded as a childhood friend from their University of Ibadan days would publicly criticise her instead of celebrating her achievement. The post Eniola Badmus apologises to Laide Bakare, calls for end to feud appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: No plot to kill Atiku, APC campaign council declares
items.description: .Says, ex-VP’s details not withdrawn By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has declared that there is no plot to assassinate former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, insisting that his security details have not been withdrawn. The council said the claim, made by a member of the ADC, Timi Frank, was false and must be proved. In a statement on Tuesday, the Spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, said: “We categorically reject the claim that the presidency of Nigeria or the APC Campaign Council is involved in any plot to assassinate former Vice President Atiku Abubakar or any opposition figure. “This is a grave allegation that Mr Frank must prove. We thus urge security agencies to invite him to substantiate the allegation, given its gravity and the urgent need to preserve life,” the statement said. The council also dismissed reports that Atiku’s security cover had been pulled. “The narrative that the security personnel attached to former Vice President Atiku have been withdrawn is totally false. The former Vice President is well protected by the police and the Department of State Security DSS. “Contrary to the falsehood promoted by Timi Frank, President Tinubu recently directed security agencies to reinforce and increase protection for all presidential, vice-presidential, governorship, and Deputy Governorship candidates across the country. “The security around the ADC Presidential candidate has never been compromised. As a former Vice President of Nigeria, he enjoys two levels of state-funded security protection. President Tinubu has increased security protection for Alhaji Atiku Abubakar as a Presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 general elections.” The campaign council, however, said it would not treat any real threat lightly. “We also urge Mr Frank not to hesitate to provide any information in his possession that will enable prompt investigation. Any credible threat to life must be treated seriously, irrespective of political affiliation,” the statement said. It described the allegation as a familiar tactic of opposition figures. “Mr Frank’s claim is typical opposition rabble-rousing meant to heat the polity. Many opposition figures, including Timi Frank, have made it a habit to write open letters and tag foreign leaders and international organisations in social media posts to draw undeserved attention to themselves,” it said. The council also pointed to the President’s own record in opposition politics. “President Bola Tinubu, as a statesman and an avowed democrat, recognises opposition politics as an essential part of our 27-year-old democracy. For 16 years in Nigeria, President Tinubu was the face of opposition, and he galvanised the opposition movement to defeat the Peoples Democratic Party as a governing party in Nigeria in 2015. “As we go deeper into the campaign season, politicians and supporters will continue to make outlandish statements and frivolous allegations to gain political advantage. “We urge candidates, political parties, and supporters to be factual and responsible in public statements and avoid utterances that can trigger avoidable tension in the polity. Let our political competition be peaceful, lawful, and focused on the big issues that matter to Nigerians, not character assassination or wild, baseless allegations”, Alake said. former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress APC, Comrade Timi Frank, has raised alarm over alleged plots to intimidate and arrest the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar, using the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC. In an open letter addressed to United States President Donald Trump and other international leaders, Frank appealed for diplomatic intervention over alleged threats to the life and political freedom of the former Vice President. Frank, who is Ambassador for East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP) and Senior Adviser to the Global Friendship City Association, United States, said the allegations required urgent and independent investigation. “These allegations must be independently and urgently investigated. Given their gravity, however, they cannot be dismissed or ignored until it is too late to prevent harm,” he said. He voiced particular concern that the EFCC could be used to initiate proceedings against Atiku in circumstances that might lead to his arrest and prolonged detention during the election campaign. “The concern is not that Atiku Abubakar should be placed above the law. The concern is that the law must never be placed at the service of political persecution. “The protection of political opposition is not a favour that any government grants at its discretion. It is a fundamental obligation of every democratic state,” he said. The post No plot to kill Atiku, APC campaign council declares appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Menace djihadiste : Rabat et Madrid appelés à renforcer leur coopération
items.description: La progression de l’organisation État islamique (EI) au Sahel et ses ambitions au-delà de la région font peser une menace croissante sur la sécurité européenne. Dans un rapport consacré à l’expansion des réseaux djihadistes, le site américain Lawfare , spécialisé dans les questions de sécurité nationale, en collaboration avec l’Institut Brookings, met en garde contre la structuration d’un corridor logistique reliant les bastions de l’organisation au Sahel au sud de l’Europe. Cette évolution, souligne le document, renforce la nécessité d’une coopération sécuritaire accrue entre le Maroc et l’Espagne. « Traiter les problèmes de sécurité dans la région du Sahel comme un problème extérieur finira inévitablement par se retourner contre l’Europe », prévient le rapport, qui appelle les pays européens à renforcer leurs dispositifs de défense face aux opérations djihadistes projetées depuis cette région. Longtemps cantonnée à une insurrection régionale, la branche sahélienne de l’État islamique, connue sous le nom d’État islamique-Province du Sahel, cherche désormais à étendre ses opérations au-delà du continent africain, jusqu’à envisager des attentats en Europe. Le parcours d’Abd Blout, un djihadiste allemand d’origine libanaise, illustre cette évolution. Après avoir tenté de se rendre en Mauritanie pour rejoindre l’organisation au Mali, il s’est dirigé vers le Liban avec le même objectif, envisageant ensuite de gagner la Syrie. En juillet dernier, il a lancé un camion de location contre une foule réunie à Berlin pour le Christopher Street Day, la marche des fiertés, avant de poursuivre son attaque au couteau. Le bilan s’est élevé à un mort et 29 blessés. Il a finalement été abattu par la police. Pour les auteurs du rapport, cet itinéraire met en lumière l’existence d’un corridor de soutien reliant les zones d’implantation de l’organisation au Mali, au Niger et au Burkina Faso à l’Espagne. Les réseaux de contrebande et les circuits extrémistes en ligne permettraient de recruter des membres, de financer les activités du groupe et de préparer des opérations des deux côtés de la Méditerranée. Si les effectifs de combattants étrangers rejoignant la Province du Sahel restent très inférieurs à ceux qui avaient afflué du monde entier pour rallier le « califat » de l’État islamique à son apogée, le groupe dispose néanmoins d’un potentiel de nuisance croissant. Le rapport estime que, dans un contexte où les services de renseignement et les forces de l’ordre concentrent leurs moyens sur d’autres menaces, cette branche pourrait être à l’origine d’un nombre accru d’attentats en Occident. Un axe maroco-espagnol sous surveillance La tentative avortée d’Abd Blout de rejoindre la Mauritanie s’inscrit, selon Lawfare, dans une dynamique plus large de déplacements de combattants étrangers vers le Sahel, suivie depuis plusieurs années par les services de renseignement marocains et espagnols. Depuis 2025, les autorités marocaines ont démantelé plusieurs cellules liées à la Province du Sahel. Parmi elles figure un réseau implanté à Tanger, accusé d’avoir financé des combattants au Sahel et en Somalie tout en préparant des attaques en Espagne. Le rapport relève également que l’État islamique appelle désormais explicitement à des attaques au Maroc, en Tunisie et en Espagne. Les liens transfrontaliers ne constituent pas un phénomène nouveau pour sa branche sahélienne. Ils étaient déjà présents dès les premières années de son développement, sous la direction de son premier émir, Adnan Abou Walid al-Sahraoui, mort en 2021. Depuis sa disparition, l’organisation a réorganisé ses structures, intégrant des membres locaux et étrangers ainsi que des responsables issus d’horizons ethniques et nationaux variés. Les groupes représentés comprennent notamment les Peuls, les Arabes, les Touareg, les Daoussahak, les Songhaï et les Zarma. Cette diversification s’accompagne d’une stratégie visant à renforcer l’implantation locale du groupe. Celui-ci cherche à se présenter comme le protecteur de populations marginalisées, notamment les Peuls, traditionnellement éleveurs et pasteurs. Il exploite ainsi les frustrations des habitants des régions défavorisées à l’égard des autorités nationales et d’autres groupes armés. Les rapports de suivi des Nations unies font état d’un renforcement de la puissance et de l’influence de l’organisation, particulièrement au Mali, favorisé en partie par cette stratégie d’ancrage local. Celle-ci lui offrirait des possibilités plus durables de recrutement et de collecte de fonds. Tanger, point de passage stratégique L’élargissement du soutien local aurait également permis à la Province du Sahel de consacrer davantage de ressources à ses opérations extérieures et d’apporter un appui à d’autres branches de l’État islamique. Dans cette stratégie, l’axe reliant le Maroc à l’Espagne occuperait une place particulière, notamment le trajet entre Tanger, le détroit de Gibraltar et les îles Baléares, identifié par les auteurs comme un corridor opérationnel. Le rapport cite deux opérations menées par les autorités marocaines en mars dernier. La première a visé la cellule dite « Tanger-Majorque ». La seconde a conduit au démantèlement d’un réseau de douze personnes affiliées à la Province du Sahel, connu sous le nom de « Lions du califat au Maghreb ». Présent dans neuf villes, ce réseau aurait cherché à établir une cellule de la branche sahélienne de l’État islamique sur le territoire marocain. Pour les auteurs, l’émergence d’un axe de circulation des combattants étrangers entre le Sahel et le sud de l’Europe représente un enjeu direct pour la sécurité du continent. Or, les dispositifs européens de lutte contre le terrorisme se sont jusqu’ici concentrés principalement sur l’État islamique-Province du Khorassan et, dans une moindre mesure, sur les autres composantes de l’organisation au Moyen-Orient. La menace en provenance du Sahel aurait, elle, bénéficié d’une attention moindre. Le rapport met enfin en garde contre les individus radicalisés, notamment les mineurs, qui parviennent à voyager vers les zones de conflit puis à en revenir en échappant à la surveillance des services de renseignement. Cette mobilité constitue, selon le document, une source persistante de préoccupation. À mesure que la Province du Sahel renforce sa capacité à inspirer, orienter et organiser des attaques, elle pourrait chercher à tirer parti des failles juridiques et opérationnelles des dispositifs européens de lutte antiterroriste. Pour les auteurs, cette perspective plaide en faveur d’une vigilance accrue et d’une coopération renforcée entre les pays situés sur les routes susceptibles d’être empruntées par les réseaux djihadistes, au premier rang desquels le Maroc et l’Espagne. #EndSARS: No Nigerian should be punished for demanding good governance – Obi
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has said no Nigerian should be punished for demanding good governance, as he marked six years since the October 20, 2020, incident at the Lekki Toll Gate. “Nigeria must become a nation where no citizen is punished for demanding good governance and a better future,” Obi said in a statement posted on X on Tuesday. Obi described the anniversary as a reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country. “Today, October 20, 2026, marks the sixth anniversary of the Lekki Toll Gate shootings, a painful reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country.” He recalled the events of October 20, 2020, saying peaceful protesters faced gunfire and that lives were lost, and many people were injured, leaving questions about justice, accountability and the value placed on human life. “On that fateful night, peaceful #EndSARS protesters were met with gunfire. Lives were lost, many were injured, and the nation was left with questions about justice, accountability, and the sanctity of human life.” Calling on Nigerians to remember the victims and resist treating injustice as normal, Obi said: “We must never forget. We must never normalise injustice.” He also noted that the anniversary reinforced his belief in a “New Nigeria,” describing it as a country where citizens are protected, young people are heard, and those in government exercise power responsibly and respect human rights. “As we remember the victims, I reaffirm my belief that a New Nigeria is possible—a country where citizens are protected, not brutalised; where young people are heard, not silenced; and where government power is exercised with responsibility and respect for human rights.” Obi added that the victims’ sacrifice should strengthen efforts to ensure the incident is not repeated while praying for those who died. “May the souls of the departed continue to rest in peace. May their sacrifice strengthen our resolve to build a Nigeria where this tragedy will never be repeated.” He ended the statement by reiterating his vision of a country where every life matters. The Lagos State Judicial Panel of Inquiry’s 2021 report found that Nigerian Army officers shot, injured and killed unarmed protesters at the Lekki Toll Gate, and said the manner of assault and killing could be described as a massacre in context. Vanguard reported that the panel identified at least 48 protesters who were shot, injured or assaulted. items.title: Sénégal : le gouvernement se dit «ouvert au dialogue et à l’apaisement» face aux appels à la grève générale
items.description: Face a la grogne sociale et aux revendications syndicales, le gouvernement senegalais a choisi de faire le point sur son action lors d'une conference de presse tenue le 19 octobre. Coordonnee par le ministre de la Fonction publique et du Travail, cette rencontre a reuni plusieurs departements ministeriels, notamment ceux de l'education nationale, de la Justice, de la Sante, de l'Enseignement superieur, de la Formation professionnelle, des Transports et du Budget. L'initiative, impulsee par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo, vise a informer l'opinion publique et a « apporter aux Senegalais et aux Senegalaises des informations claires sur les efforts engages par le gouvernement en reponse aux revendications des travailleurs », a indique le porte-parole du gouvernement, Bakary Sarr. Selon la presse senegalaise, cette demarche fait suite a une reunion du comite de pilotage du Pacte national de stabilite sociale pour une croissance inclusive et le developpement, tenue le 15 octobre sous la presidence du chef du gouvernement. Le porte-parole a souligne que cet exercice repondait a une exigence de transparence et de redevabilite, permettant de dresser un etat precis de l'avancement des mesures engagees, ministere par ministere. Il a egalement renouvele l'appel aux centrales syndicales a poursuivre la concertation dans un climat social apaise. « Le gouvernement demeure ouvert au dialogue et a l'apaisement. Notre priorite est de poursuivre les echanges dans un esprit de responsabilite, de recherche de solutions dans l'interet des travailleurs comme de l'ensemble de la population », a-t-il affirme. Le Front syndical appelle a une greve generale, le gouvernement plaide pour sa suspension Le Front syndical pour la defense des travailleurs (FSDT), collectif regroupant treize syndicats de differents secteurs, a appele a une marche le 20 octobre, suivie d'une greve generale de trois jours a partir du 21 octobre. La mobilisation concerne notamment les secteurs de l'education, de la sante, de l'enseignement superieur et de l'electricite. Les syndicats reclament l'application des accords conclus pour ameliorer les conditions de travail et repondre aux revendications salariales. La revalorisation des pensions de retraite, le relevement de l'âge obligatoire de depart a la retraite de 60 a 65 ans, le versement de primes ainsi que la generalisation de l'indemnite de logement a 100 000 francs CFA figurent egalement parmi les revendications. Cet appel a la greve intervient a quelques jours de l'ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar 2026, prevus du 31 octobre au 13 novembre. Une edition historique pour le Senegal et le continent africain, qui accueillera pour la premiere fois une manifestation olympique. De son cote, Mamadou Lamine Diante, ministre de la Fonction publique, du Travail et de la Reforme du service public, a solennellement appele le FSDT a suspendre son mouvement au profit de la concertation. Affirmant que le pays etait « encore loin du point de rupture », il a reitere la disposition du gouvernement a rechercher des solutions. Cet appel fait suite a une demande formulee la semaine precedente par le Premier ministre, qui avait invite les syndicats a observer un moratoire de trois mois sur les greves, dans un contexte de difficultes financieres persistantes.

items.title: Un bilan marqué par des panels riches en enseignements
items.description: Le président de la Coordination des élèves et étudiants ressortissants de Ndiandiaye-Fatick (CEERNF) est revenu, lundi 19 octobre 2026 sur le bilan de la vingt-troisième édition des cours de vacances qu'ils organisent chaque année au quartier Ndiandiaye de Fatick. Daouda Marone s'est félicité du programme et particulièrement de la journée de clôture où plusieurs thèmes ont été abordés en présence des élèves et parents du quartier. FATICK- Après la cérémonie de clôture de la vingt-troisième édition des cours de vacances organisés par la Coordination des élèves et étudiants ressortissants de Ndiandiaye-Fatick (CEERNF), l'heure est au bilan. Lundi 19 octobre 2026, le président de la structure, Daouda Marone, est revenu sur les points saillants de ce programme qui a mobilisé un total de cinq cent vingt-cinq (525) élèves, de la classe de CI à la Terminale. Trois thèmes ont fait l'objet de réflexion durant la cérémonie de clôture effectuée à l'école élémentaire Ngor Ndam Ndiaye du quartier Ndiandiaye de Fatick. D'abord sur le pétrole de Sangomar avec comme conférencier Boubacar Mbodj, ministre conseiller chargé des questions énergétiques au temps du président Macky Sall. Ce thème traitait des impacts de l'exploitation de la ressource pétrolière dans la région de Fatick. En outre, d’autres panels ont été aussi consacrés à la protection de l'environnement, mais surtout à l'utilisation responsable du téléphone par les élèves. Il s'agit là d'une invite aux apprenants à utiliser à bon escient cet appareil portable. Cependant, avant la cérémonie de clôture, d'autres journées ont marqué l'édition de cette année. “Dans le cadre de notre programme, nous avons eu à organiser une journée de reboisement avec trois cents (300) arbres plantés. Il y a eu aussi une activité de dons de sang où nous avons récolté 50 poches, ce qui est un record à Fatick. Sans oublier également l'installation de bancs écologiques et la mise en place d’un jardin public à l'école Ngor Ndam Ndiaye”, s'est félicité M. Marrone. Le président de la (CEERNF) n'a surtout pas oublié d'évoquer les difficultés rencontrées, essentiellement d'ordre financier. Il a ainsi lancé un appel aux autorités locales afin qu'elles s'impliquent dans ce programme annuel qui aide les élèves à mieux préparer l'année scolaire. El hadji Fodé SARR (Correspondant)

items.title: AfricaRice renforce la filière semencière rizicole ouest-africaine
items.description: Dans le cadre du programme REWARD, AfricaRice organise du 19 au 23 octobre 2026 à Saint-Louis un atelier de formation de formateurs issus de 13 pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest. L’initiative vise à améliorer la production de semences de riz de qualité, à renforcer les compétences techniques et à contribuer à la réduction des importations. L’accès à des semences de qualité constitue un enjeu majeur pour accroître la production rizicole et renforcer la souveraineté alimentaire en Afrique de l’Ouest. C’est dans cette perspective qu’AfricaRice organise, du 19 au 23 octobre 2026, à sa Station régionale du Sahel, à Saint-Louis, un atelier consacré aux techniques de production de semences de riz hybrides et de variétés fixées. Cette formation s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme REWARD, qui fédère treize pays autour du transfert de technologies, de l’harmonisation des pratiques et du renforcement de la chaîne de valeur du riz. Pour Traoré Valentin Stanislas Edgar, coordinateur du projet REWARD AfricaRice, la coopération régionale est essentielle pour relever les défis de la production. « L’objectif de ce projet est de voir comment, ensemble, nous pouvons trouver des solutions pour réduire les importations à travers la production locale », a-t-il souligné. Il estime que les variétés améliorées et résilientes au changement climatique, associées aux bonnes pratiques agricoles, peuvent aider les producteurs à faire face à la sécheresse, aux inondations, aux maladies et aux ravageurs. Le programme entend également promouvoir des variétés adaptées aux conditions locales et aux préférences des consommateurs. Dr Seydou Bah, coordinateur de l’unité semences à AfricaRice, rappelle l’objectif de la rencontre : « Le but de cet atelier, c’est de former nos partenaires au niveau des pays à la production de semences de riz de haute qualité » Les participants sont appelés à transmettre leurs connaissances à d’autres acteurs dans leurs pays respectifs. Les modules abordent notamment la multiplication des semences, la conduite des cultures, la gestion de l’eau et de la fertilisation, ainsi que les techniques de récolte et de post-récolte. Une attention particulière est également accordée à la participation des femmes, afin de favoriser une meilleure inclusion dans la filière semencière. À travers cette approche, AfricaRice ambitionne de consolider un réseau ouest-africain de formateurs et de contribuer à la disponibilité de semences performantes, indispensables à l’amélioration des rendements et au développement durable de la riziculture. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: GoldBod targets bigger stake for Ghana in new mines through geological studies
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is undertaking geological investigations in parts of the country to reduce investment risks and position Ghana to secure stronger equity stakes in future mining projects, Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi has announced. Mr Gyamfi said the board was collaborating with the Ghana Geological Survey Authority under its Mining Support Programme to investigate mineralised areas at Funsi in the Upper West Region and Bensere in the Ashanti Region. The studies are expected to provide reliable geological data, attract credible investors and support the responsible expansion of Ghana’s mining base. Delivering a keynote address at the African Minerals Policy Forum – Mining in Motion 2026, Mr Gyamfi said the initiative was intended to address one of the major barriers to greater Ghanaian participation in the mining industry: the risk capital required for geological exploration. He argued that mineral sovereignty must extend beyond legal ownership of resources to effective local participation in financing, technology, processing and mining operations. “These studies will help build a reliable investment-grade asset portfolio, reduce investor risks and position GoldBod to negotiate stronger equity stakes in the resulting model mines for Ghana,” he said. Mr Gyamfi added that the country needed to move away from overdependence on free-carried interests and royalties towards securing controlling equity interests in sustainable mines.

items.title: GoldBod reforms recover gold worth $11.4bn previously lost through trade leakages – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has highlighted the scale of gold trade leakages Ghana faced before the introduction of reforms to formalise the artisanal and small-scale mining sector. Mr Gyamfi cited a SWISSAID analysis of UN Comtrade mirror data which found a 229-tonne gap, valued at approximately US$11.4 billion, between Ghana’s reported gold exports and the corresponding imports declared by its trading partners from 2019 to 2023. He said the discrepancy illustrated how substantial volumes of Ghanaian gold had escaped official export records and the country’s foreign exchange system. Speaking at the African Minerals Policy Forum – Mining in Motion 2026, he also recalled that recorded small-scale gold exports fell from 75.7 tonnes in 2018 to 53.4 tonnes in 2019 and 39.3 tonnes in 2020. Following the introduction of a three per cent withholding tax on unprocessed small-scale gold, official exports plunged to 3.4 tonnes in 2021, worth US$185 million. “The gold beneath our soil had not disappeared, nor had production stopped; the trade had simply moved beyond official view,” Mr Gyamfi said. He attributed the leakages to fragmented trading arrangements, weak regulatory oversight and ineffective aggregation and foreign exchange repatriation systems, arguing that GoldBod’s reforms were designed to bring more of the country’s gold trade into the formal economy and ensure greater benefits for Ghanaians.

items.title: Police disrupt #EndSARS memorial at Lekki tollgate, tear gas Rhodes-Vivour, Doherty
items.description: By Esther Onyegbula Police officers on Tuesday fired tear gas to disperse residents, journalists, activists and political figures gathered at the Lekki tollgate in Lagos to commemorate victims of the October 2020 #EndSARS protests. Among those affected by the police action were the Lagos State governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty. The memorial, organised by the Enough is Enough movement, was aimed at honouring those who lost their lives during the #EndSARS protests and remembering the nationwide demonstrations against police brutality. The gathering was, however, disrupted before participants could lay wreaths at the tollgate, as police officers deployed to the venue fired tear gas canisters to disperse the crowd. The action triggered confusion as participants scrambled for safety amid clouds of tear gas that spread across the area. Following the incident, participants fled the scene as the gas filled the vicinity, forcing the disruption of the planned commemoration. The memorial was part of activities to remember the victims of the #EndSARS protests, which drew widespread public attention in October 2020 over allegations of police brutality, particularly against young Nigerians. The Lekki tollgate became a focal point of the protests and has remained a significant site for subsequent commemorations by activists and other Nigerians demanding accountability, justice and reforms in the country’s policing system. Tuesday’s incident prevented participants from completing the planned wreath-laying ceremony, which was intended to pay tribute to those who lost their lives during the protests. Meanwhile, the Lagos State Police Command is yet to provide an explanation for the use of tear gas at the time of filing this report.
